title: MOSIP-44259: PMS - OIDC flow fails due to unresolved eSignet mapping file URLs
content:
Problem description:
While testing the *OIDC flow*, OIDC client creation fails with a *500 Internal Server Error*.
The issue occurs because the required *eSignet mapping file URLs are not resolved*, causing PMS to fail while fetching configuration files from the *mosip-config (*https://github.com/mosip/mosip-config/blob/dev/partner-management-default.properties#L319).

esignet claims mapping file url

{{mosip.pms.esignet.claims-mapping-file-url=${spring_config_url_env}/application/${active_profile_env}/${spring_config_label_env}/identity-mapping.json}}

esignet amr-acr mapping file url

{{mosip.pms.esignet.amr-acr-mapping-file-url=${spring_config_url_env}/application/${active_profile_env}/${spring_config_label_env}/amr-acr-mapping.json}}

After updating the configuration to use *raw GitHub URLs*, the issue is resolved and the OIDC flow works successfully.
`mosip.pms.esignet.claims-mapping-file-url=`
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mosip/mosip-config/refs/heads/dev/identity-mapping.json`

`mosip.pms.esignet.amr-acr-mapping-file-url=`
`https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mosip/mosip-config/refs/heads/dev/amr-acr-mapping.json`

title: MOSIP-44260: In mosip Data repo workflow currently deletes and recreates the CSV directory on every push commits run, which makes it appear like CSVs are added each time.
content:
Problem description:
The GitHub Actions workflow responsible for converting `.xlsx` files to `.csv` is currently *deleting and recreating the CSV output directory on every workflow run*.

Because of this, even when there are *no changes in the XLSX files*, the workflow still removes the existing CSV folder and regenerates the CSV files. This makes it look like CSV files are “added again” on every PR push/synchronize event.

There is change in repo tree structure as well, check and update the workflow accordigly

title: MOSIP-24211: Single point of failure with config-server (No pod priority )
content:
Problem description:
## ⚠️ *Problem Summary*

- You have *only 1 replica (pod)* of Config Server

- *No pod priority / scheduling rules*

- If:
** Node goes down
** Pod gets evicted
** Rolling update happens

👉 *Entire system may fail to fetch configs → cascading failures*

----

## 🧱 *How SPOF Happens*

```App Pods  ---> Config Server (1 pod) ❌
                |
             Node Down
                ↓
         No Config → App crash
```

----

## ✅ *Solution: Make Config Server Highly Available*

### 1. 🔁 *Increase Replicas*

```replicas: 2  # minimum
```

👉 Recommended:

- *2 replicas* → minimum HA

- *3 replicas* → production-grade

----

### 2. 🧠 *Pod Anti-Affinity (CRITICAL)*

Ensure pods are NOT on the same node:

```affinity:
  podAntiAffinity:
    requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:

      - labelSelector:
          matchLabels:
            app: config-server
        topologyKey: "kubernetes.io/hostname"
```

👉 Prevents both pods landing on same node

----

### 3. 🚨 *Pod Priority Class*

Create high priority:

```apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: high-priority
value: 100000
globalDefault: false
description: "Critical system component"
```

Attach to deployment:

```priorityClassName: high-priority
```

👉 Ensures:

- Config server pods are *not evicted first*

----

### 4. 🔄 *Pod Disruption Budget (PDB)*

```apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: config-server-pdb
spec:
  minAvailable: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: config-server
```

👉 Prevents:

- Both pods getting killed during maintenance

----

### 5. ❤️ *Liveness & Readiness Probes*

```livenessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /actuator/health
    port: 8888
  initialDelaySeconds: 30
  periodSeconds: 10

readinessProbe:
  httpGet:
    path: /actuator/health
    port: 8888
  initialDelaySeconds: 20
  periodSeconds: 5
```

👉 Ensures traffic only goes to healthy pods

----

### 6. ⚖️ *Service Load Balancing*

Make sure you use:

```type: ClusterIP
```

And access via:

```http://config-server:8888
```

👉 Kubernetes will load balance across pods

### *Upgrade Deployment(upgrading eSignet to new version):*

Steps to be followed if the user is trying to upgrade the eSignet to the newer version:

*Steps to upgrade:*

1. Run upgrade-all.sh file to upgrade eSignet version:
## `./upgrade-all.sh` (We should check if we can only deploy folder to be downloaded and cloning and other things script takes care user )

### [“eSignetbackup“] = “Please confirm with 'y' to start the back up process: “(Check if this can be done with the script)

#### Once user confirms the process to start the back up, user should be displayed with the information on what is getting backed up in form of running comments and total progress
### Upgrade process should start, if in any case the upgrade is halted for any unseen circumstances, script should be able to start the rollback
### If user halts the upgrade process then user should have option to manually initiate the rollback process to the current version of the eSignet that user has

title: MOSIP-41451: Missing UUID Mapping in Terraform Script for /etc/fstab – Causes Volume Mount Failure on Reboot
content:
Problem description:
The Terraform module for AWS resource creation in the https://github.com/mosip/infra-priv/blob/3df7a03bb42367a98a4024bcb948a5eca5fc414d/terraform/modules/aws/aws-resource-creation/variables.tf#L115 currently does *not configure the UUID of the attached storage device* (e.g., `/dev/nvme1n1`) in `/etc/fstab`.

Due to this, when the instance is rebooted, *device names may change dynamically*, leading to incorrect or failed mounts for critical volumes (e.g., `/srv/nfs`). This recently resulted in *data inaccessibility for NFS clients*, impacting dependent services.

*Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Provision an instance using the current Terraform module.

1. Mount the attached volume using device name (e.g., `/dev/nvme1n1`) without referencing UUID.

1. Reboot the instance.

1. Observe mount failure and data inaccessibility due to incorrect device mapping.

*Expected Behavior:*
The Terraform provisioner should:

- Retrieve the UUID of the attached block device using `blkid`.

- Automatically update `/etc/fstab` using the UUID (not the device name) to ensure persistent and reliable mounts.

title: MOSIP-43063: Optimize Keycloak Postgres queries by adding targeted indexes
content:
Problem description:
*Description*
We observed slow response times (~6s) for single-user fetches on the `/userdetails` path, with p90 latency around 5–7s. Investigation showed that the Auth → Keycloak user-lookup path was the bottleneck due to inefficient Postgres queries and missing indexes.

*What we saw*

- Sync service timers indicated the Keycloak DB leg dominated total request time.

- Queries without `realm_id` filters caused Postgres to fall back to sequential scans instead of using existing composite indexes.

- Example (before optimization):

```EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)
SELECT ue.username, ue.email
FROM public.user_entity ue
WHERE ue.username = 'performance';

-- Result: Seq Scan ... ~8 ms, but cumulative impact under load ~6s
```

- After adding indexes, query planner switched to index scans (~0.05 ms).

*Root cause*

- Missing targeted indexes on frequently accessed columns.

- Chatty Auth → Keycloak API usage patterns (list-then-filter, multiple per-user role lookups).

*Fix implemented*
Added the following *non-blocking concurrent indexes* in production:

```CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_entity_username
  ON public.user_entity (username);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_attr_userid_name
  ON public.user_attribute (user_id, name);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_attr_userpassword
  ON public.user_attribute (user_id) WHERE name = 'userPassword';

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_credential_user_id
  ON public.credential (user_id);

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_role_user
  ON public.user_role_mapping (user_id);
```

*Impact*

- Reduced `/userdetails` p90 latency from 5–7s → ~0.8–1.0s.

- Single-user fetches are now sub-second.

- DB IO load decreased (no full scans).

- Auth/Keycloak CPU usage reduced due to fewer HTTP calls.

*Verification*

- Verified via `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE)` → index scans used across target queries.

- Service logs show improved timings: single-user fetch now ;}}.

- Application changes backward-compatible (fallback to old fetch path if required).

*Follow-ups*

- Consider adding trigram GIN index for fuzzy search endpoints:

```CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pg_trgm;
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS idx_user_username_trgm
  ON public.user_entity USING gin (username gin_trgm_ops);
```

- Add Grafana dashboards to monitor:
** Auth/Keycloak API latency
** Token reuse / refresh rates
** Postgres index hit ratios, slow query logs

title: MOSIP-42975: Enhancement in helm chart
content:
Problem description:
lifecycle: preStop: exec: command: ["sleep", "10"] after startupProbe: what is use of it

What actually happens on termination

1. Kubernetes starts terminating the pod → *runs* `preStop` *first*.

1. While `preStop` runs (your `sleep 10`), the pod is marked *Terminating* and is *removed from Service endpoints* (readiness goes false). Traffic _should_ stop being routed to it, but there’s a small propagation delay.

1. After `preStop` finishes, kubelet sends *SIGTERM* to the container. Then your app’s *graceful shutdown* begins (e.g., `server.shutdown=graceful`).

1. If the app hasn’t exited by `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`, kubelet sends *SIGKILL*.

Why the sleep helps

- It gives *10s for the load balancer/endpoints to drain*, so *no new* requests arrive before SIGTERM.

- Any *in-flight* requests can complete during this pause, reducing errors like “Interrupted during connection acquisition”.

Notes

- YAML order (preStop appearing after startupProbe) doesn’t affect semantics—they’re separate features:
** *startupProbe*: only during startup.
** *preStop*: only during shutdown/drain.

- 10s is okay; many teams use *20–30s* depending on LB propagation and request duration. Pair it with a larger `terminationGracePeriodSeconds` (e.g., *60s*) so the app then has time to do its graceful shutdown after the drain pause.

*Rule of thumb:*
 `preStop sleep ≈ LB drain time` → then *SIGTERM* → app graceful shutdown within `terminationGracePeriodSeconds`.

title: MOSIP-44213: minio data backup and restore activity.
content:
Problem description:
we have seen that when using mc client for minio data backup and restore the objects doesn't have metadata after restoring so need to RnD on the same to make sure the objects have metadat after restoring the minio data.

Discussion and resolution:
[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Mohan E commented: We are facing an error while upgrading minio version from 10.1.6 to 15.0.6 i,e {{FATAL Unable to use the drive /bitnami/minio/data: drive not found: Invalid arguments specified}} usually indicates a *breaking change in how MinIO handles data storage* between your old version (10.1.6) and the new version (15.0.6).

In late 2022, MinIO removed support for the legacy "Filesystem" (FS) mode. Newer versions now require the data to be in the "Single-Node Single-Drive" (SNSD) format. If you mount a volume containing the old FS-style data to a new MinIO container, it will fail to start because it doesn't recognize the old structure as a valid MinIO drive.

h3. The Problem: Legacy FS vs. SNSD

* *Version 10.1.6 (Old):* Used a simpler directory structure.
* *Version 15.0.6 (New):* Expects a {{.minio.sys}} metadata directory formatted for the new backend.
* *Bitnami Specifics:* Bitnami containers run as non-root (UID 1001). If the folder permissions on your "rescued" PVC are still owned by the old user or root, the container cannot initialize the new metadata, leading to the "drive not found" error.

cc: [~accountid:5d4159ed4125b20c3159b1ed] [~accountid:712020:d3c2f437-f0b7-4582-b791-2801ccb3eb83]

[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Mohan E commented: things that were tried:

* preserve option  ---> still not able to retrieve metadata
* replicate option ---> need multiple servers i,e older version and uograde version to be live at the sametime to work.
* minio upgrade ---> upgrade is done from older version to latest version but the pod fails to come up because, In late 2022, MinIO removed support for the legacy "Filesystem" (FS) mode. Newer versions now require the data to be in the "Single-Node Single-Drive" (SNSD) format. If you mount a volume containing the old FS-style data to a new MinIO container, it will fail to start because it doesn't recognize the old structure as a valid MinIO drive.

[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Mohan E commented: GPT suggestions: 

h3. The Solution: The "Sidecar" Migration

Since you cannot simply "point" the new version at the old data, you must perform a data migration.

h4. 1. Temporarily Roll Back to a "Bridge" Version

You need a running MinIO instance to "get the data out." Install a version close to your original that is compatible with the old data.

* *Option A:* Reinstall the 10.1.6 chart using your existing PVC.
* *Option B:* Spin up a standalone pod using the old image just to access the files.

h4. 2. Use {{mc mirror}} to Move Data

Once the old MinIO is running and you can see your files:

# *Deploy a "Clean" MinIO 15.0.6* with a *NEW, empty PVC*.
# *Use the MinIO Client (*{{mc}}*)* to sync data from the old one to the new one.

{noformat}Bash{noformat}

{noformat}# Example commands using the MinIO Client (mc)
mc alias set old_minio http://old-minio-svc:9000 admin password
mc alias set new_minio http://new-minio-svc:9000 admin password

# Sync all buckets and data
mc mirror old_minio new_minio{noformat}


But for us the above suggestion won’t work because using mc client to mirror data will lead to loss of metadata of objects which is necessary for us.

title: MOSIP-44736: Keycloak client secrets overwritten with empty values during eSignet prerequisite initialization
labels: bug, github_movement_2026, DST-Engg, devops, devops_gh, dst-1-2-1-0, devsecops
content:
Problem description:
*Description:*

During eSignet prerequisite initialization (`initialise-prereq.sh` → `keycloak-init.sh`), the script overwrites the existing `keycloak-client-secrets` in the `keycloak` namespace with empty values. Additionally, the `keycloak-client-secrets` is not consistently created in the `esignet` namespace.

This issue occurs when deploying *eSignet* alongside an *existing MOSIP Platform* deployment and affects all tested eSignet versions (v1.5.0 → v1.7.1). As a result, MOSIP clients *(PMS, IDA, Deployment-client, mPartner-default-auth & mPartner-default-mobile)* fail authentication, and eSignet clients may not initialize properly.

*Affected Versions:*

- eSignet v1.5.0 → v1.7.1

- MOSIP Platform (pre-deployed)

*Steps to Reproduce:*

1. Deploy MOSIP Platform with Keycloak initialized.

1. Run eSignet prerequisites:
```./initialise-prereq.sh [kubeconfig]
```

1. Select `y` to initialize Keycloak.

1. Inspect secrets:
```kubectl -n keycloak get secret keycloak-client-secrets -o yaml
kubectl -n esignet get secret keycloak-client-secrets -o yaml
```

*Expected Result:*

- Existing MOSIP Keycloak client secrets remain intact in Keycloak Namespace.

- eSignet clients are created without overwriting existing secrets.

- `keycloak-client-secrets` exists correctly in the `esignet` namespace.

*Actual Result:*

- Secret values in `keycloak-client-secrets` are overwritten with empty values (`""`) in Keycloak Namespace

- `keycloak-client-secrets` is not created in the `esignet` namespace

- Leads to authentication failures in dependent services 

*Root Cause Analysis:*

1. `keycloak-init.sh` uses incorrect variable references (e.g., `.data.$DEPLOYMENT_CLIENT_SECRET_VALUE` instead of `.data.$DEPLOYMENT_CLIENT_SECRET_KEY`).

1. The script overwrites secrets without checking for empty values.

1. Cross-namespace secret copy (`$COPY_UTIL`) may fail silently.

1. Helm job failures during Keycloak initialization are not properly handled.

## 📎 Attachments

- [eSignet-Keycloak-init.PNG](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/MOSIP-44736)

title: MOSIP-44389: Env creation handover through rapid deployment to Dev, QA
content:
Problem description:
As a *DevOps team*,
we want to *handover environment creation using Rapid Deployment to Dev and QA teams*,
so that *Dev and QA environments can be provisioned quickly, consistently, and with minimal manual intervention*, *dependency.*

This story covers documenting, validating, and handing over the Rapid Deployment process for creating Dev and QA environments, including access, prerequisites, and troubleshooting guidance.

### *Acceptance Criteria*

- Rapid Deployment process for *Dev* environment is documented and verified

- Rapid Deployment process for *QA* environment is documented and verified

- All required *inputs, configurations, and prerequisites* are clearly documented

- Environment creation steps are reproducible without devops team involvement

- Access permissions for Dev & QA teams are validated

- Rollback and failure-handling steps are documented

- Handover walkthrough session completed with Dev & QA teams

- Sign-off received from Dev & QA representatives

----

### *Scope / Inclusions*

- Dev & QA environment provisioning

- Rapid Deployment scripts/pipelines

- Configuration parameters

- Secrets and access handling (high level)

- Validation checklist post deployment

### *Dependencies*

- Rapid Deployment pipelines/scripts available and stable

- Required cloud/K8s access configured

- Secrets and credentials provisioned

----

### *Tasks*

1. Review existing Rapid Deployment setup

1. Finalize Dev environment deployment steps

1. Finalize QA environment deployment steps

1. Create handover documentation

1. Validate access for Dev & QA teams

1. Conduct knowledge transfer session

1. Collect sign-off

labels: bug, github_movement_2026, DST-Engg, devops, devops_gh, dst-1-2-1-0, devsecops
content:
Problem description:
During the installation of config-server, the `install.sh` script prompts:

```Do
you want to enable config-server to pull configurations from multiple repositories? (Y/n) (Default: n)
```

When the user inputs `n`, the generated Kubernetes ConfigMap `config-server-env-vars` is created but contains *no data entries at all* (completely empty).

This results in:

- Config-server having no information on Git repository URI or search paths so config-server pod getting multiple restarts not coming up.

- Failure to pull configuration properties from any Git repository

- Application configuration fetch failures during runtime

title: MOSIP-44794: Deployment Failures and Documentation Mismatch in k8s-infra v1.2.1.1 & v1.2.1.0
labels: bug, github_movement_2026, DST-Engg, devops, devops_gh, dst-1-2-1-0, devsecops
content:
Problem description:
### *Environment:*

- Component: k8s-infra

- Versions: v1.2.1.0, v1.2.1.1

- MOSIP GitHub repository:
[[https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/v1.2.1.1](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/v1.2.1.1|smart-link)](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/v1.2.1.1](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/tree/v1.2.1.1|smart-link)) 

### *Description:*

There are multiple inconsistencies between the documentation and actual script behavior during the setup of infrastructure components such as NFS, Istio, RKE2 cluster, and Nginx. These issues lead to confusion and failed executions when following the documented steps.

*Issues Identified:*

#### *1. RKE2 Cluster Setup – Invalid Hostname Format in Documentation*

*Document Reference:* `host.ini.sample`

*Issue:*
The sample hostname provided:

```control-subsequent_plane-1
```

contains an underscore (`_`), which causes the cluster creation to fail.

*Observed Behavior:*

- Cluster setup fails when using the documented hostname. 

*Expected Behavior:*

- Hostnames should follow valid naming conventions (no underscores). 

*Workaround:*

- Changing the hostname to: 

```control-subsequent-plane-1
```

allows successful cluster creation.

*Error Observed:*

```fatal: [control-subsequent_plane-1]: FAILED! => {
  "msg": "The task includes an option with an undefined variable.. 
```

#### *2. Istio Ingress Installation – Missing CRDs Dependency Not Documented*

*Issue:*
While installing Istio ingress, the following errors are observed:

```no matches for kind "PodMonitor" in version "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"
no matches for kind "ServiceMonitor" in version "monitoring.coreos.com/v1"
ensure CRDs are installed first
```

*Observed Behavior:*

- Script throws errors related to missing CRDs. 

- However, pods in `istio-system` namespace are still up and running. 

*Expected Behavior:*

- Installation should complete without errors when following documented steps. 

*Root Cause / Finding:*

- Required CRDs ([monitoring.coreos.com](http://monitoring.coreos.com)) are not installed prior to Istio setup. 

*Workaround:*

- Install `cattle-monitoring-system` before installing Istio. 

- After this, the script executes successfully without errors. 

*Documentation Gap:*

- Current documentation places monitoring setup after Istio installation, which is incorrect. 

#### *3. NFS Server & Client Setup – Mismatch Between Documentation and Script*

##### *NFS Server Installation*

*Document Says:*

- User must provide environment name.

- Expected path:

```/srv/nfs/mosip/
```

*Observed Behavior:*

- Script uses `/srv/nfs` directly. 

- No prompt for {{}}. 

- Installation completes successfully without environment input. 

*Issue:*

- Documentation does not match actual script behavior. 

##### *NFS Client Installation*

*Document Says:*
 User will be prompted for:

```Please provide NFS SERVER: 
Please provide NFS Path: 
```

*Observed Behavior:*

- Script fails with error: 

```./install-nfs-csi.sh: line 21: NFS_SERVER: unbound variable
```

*Expected Behavior:*

- Script should prompt for required inputs or handle missing variables gracefully. 

#### *StorageClass Configuration Mismatch (Volume Expansion Disabled)*

*Documentation States:*
Post-installation expected output:

```NAME        PROVISIONER              RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION
nfs-csi     cluster.local/nfs-csi    Retain          Immediate           true
```

----

*Actual Observed Output:*

```NAME                PROVISIONER      RECLAIMPOLICY   VOLUMEBINDINGMODE   ALLOWVOLUMEEXPANSION
nfs-csi (default)   nfs.csi.k8s.io   Delete          Immediate           false
```

#### *Post Installation Validation Command Mismatch*

*Documentation States:*
 Check deployment:

```kubectl
-n nfs get deployment.apps/csi-driver-nfs
```

*Actual Observed Behavior:*

```kubectl get deploy -n nfs

NAME                 READY   UP-TO-DATE   AVAILABLE
csi-nfs-controller   1/1     1            1kubectl
-n nfs get deployment.apps/csi-nfs-controller
```

*Findings:*

- Deployment name differs: 
** *Documented:* `csi-driver-nfs` 
** *Actual:* `csi-nfs-controller` 

#### *4. Nginx Setup – Incorrect Host Group in Sample Configuration*

*Document Reference:* `hosts.ini.sample`

*Sample Provided:*

```[cluster]
node1 ansible_host= ansible_user=root ansible_ssh_private_key_file=
```

*Observed Behavior:*

- Script execution fails with: 

```skipping: no hosts matched
```

*Expected Behavior:*

- Script should execute successfully using provided sample configuration. 

*Workaround:*

- Changing the host group from `[cluster]` to `[nginx]` allows successful execution.

*5. Cattle-logging-system:*

The cattle-logging-system deployment is failing in the Kubernetes cluster, where all Elasticsearch-related pods are stuck in `CrashLoopBackOff` or `Init:CrashLoopBackOff` state. This issue is reproducible on both Ubuntu 22.04 and Ubuntu 24.04 nodes.

- OS: *Ubuntu 22.04 LTS, Ubuntu 24.04 LTS*

- Elasticsearch Image: mosipint/elasticsearch:7.17.2-debian-10-r4
** init-containerImage: [mosipint/os-shell:12-debian-12-r46](http://docker.io/mosipint/os-shell:12-debian-12-r46)

- Kibana Image: mosipint/kibana:7.17.2-debian-10-r0

*Actual Result:*
Elasticsearch container fails during startup with the following error:

```Exception in thread "main" java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "jdk.internal.platform.CgroupInfo.getMountPoint()" because "anyController" is null
    at jdk.internal.platform.cgroupv2.CgroupV2Subsystem.getInstance(...)
    at jdk.internal.platform.CgroupSubsystemFactory.create(...)
    at jdk.internal.platform.CgroupMetrics.getInstance(...)
    ...
```

### *Impact:*

- Users face failures and confusion when following official documentation. 

- Additional troubleshooting required, increasing setup time. 

- Potential blocker for new deployments. 

### *Expected Resolution:*

- Align documentation with actual script behavior. 

- Fix script inconsistencies where applicable. 

- Update setup sequence (for monitoring and Istio dependencies if required).

## 📎 Attachments

title: Partner Onboarder: Jobs fail due to unknown MOSIP root CA (v3)
content:
Problem description:
When installing the partner onboarder, at the end the demo jobs are run. In the generated reports it turns out that checks fail. It seems like the jobs try to upload certificates as intermediate CA. However their root CA is not present in the partner management, so that the intermediate certificates are rejected.

It looks to me like this is a general problem not related to the system running in an internal network.

I have eventually been able to work around this problem by downloading the root certificate and then uploading it to the partner management. However the solution is rather ugly, because the partner management services need to be up in order for this to succeed, and as the jobs are run within the same `helm` call as the installation, there's a bit of a chicken-egg problem.

The solution is to run `helm` twice: once for installation only, no jobs, then again for the jobs. Hence there's 2 `values.yaml` files.

`values-bootstrap.yaml` is for installation only, all jobs disabled (the first 3 blocks are workarounds for the use of a corporate CA as described in #1714, may not be relevant for everybody):
```yaml
extraEnvVars:
  - name: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
    value: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem

extraVolumes:
  - name: corporate-ca
    secret:
      secretName: corporate-ca

extraVolumeMounts:
  - name: corporate-ca
    mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
    subPath: corporate-ca.pem
    readOnly: true

onboarding:
  modules:
    - name: ida
      enabled: false
    - name: print
      enabled: false
    - name: abis
      enabled: false
    - name: resident
      enabled: false
    - name: digitalcard
      enabled: false
```

The file `values.yaml` is identical, just every onboarding module's `enabled` set to `true`.

Then split the `helm` calls in `install.sh` and add code for downloading / uploading the certificate (the `--post-renderer` arguments are workarounds for the use of a corporate CA as described in #1714, may not be relevant for everybody):

```shell
  echo Install onboarding module
  helm -n $NS install partner-onboarder mosip/partner-onboarder \
  $NFS_OPTION \
  $S3_OPTION \
  --set onboarding.variables.push_reports_to_s3=$push_reports_to_s3 \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[0]=global \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[1]=keycloak-env-vars \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[2]=keycloak-host \
  $ENABLE_INSECURE \
  -f values-bootstrap.yaml \
  --version $CHART_VERSION \
  --wait-for-jobs \
  --post-renderer ./post-render.sh


  API_HOST="$(kubectl -n onboarder get configmap global -o jsonpath='{.data.mosip-api-internal-host}')"
  CLIENT_SECRET="$(kubectl -n onboarder get secret keycloak-client-secrets -o jsonpath='{.data}' | jq | grep mosip_deployment_client_secret | awk '{ print $2 }' | tr -d '",' | base64 -d)"
  AUTH_JSON="{
  \"id\":\"string\",
  \"metadata\":{},
  \"request\":{
    \"appId\":\"ida\",
    \"clientId\":\"mosip-deployment-client\",
    \"secretKey\":\"$CLIENT_SECRET\"
  },
  \"requesttime\":\"2026-04-08T09:43:52.913Z\",
  \"version\":\"string\"
}"
  echo 1>&2
  echo

  echo Download session cookie to headers.txt:
  curl -sk -D headers.txt -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d "$AUTH_JSON" "https://${API_HOST}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/clientidsecretkey"
  SESSION_COOKIE="$(grep -i '^set-cookie: Authorization=' headers.txt | sed 's/^set-cookie: //I' | cut -d';' -f1)"
  echo 1>&2
  echo

  echo Download root-ca.pem:
  curl -sk -H "Cookie: $SESSION_COOKIE" "https://${API_HOST}/v1/keymanager/getCertificate?applicationId=ROOT" | jq .response.certificate | perl -pe 's/"//g; s/\\n/\n/g' >root-ca.pem
  echo 1>&2
  echo

  echo Upload root-ca.pem, ignore KER-PCM-003 if it is already there:
  curl -sk -X POST "https://${API_HOST}/v1/partnermanager/partners/certificate/ca/upload" -H "Cookie: $SESSION_COOKIE" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @- <<EOF
{
  "id": "string",
  "metadata": {},
  "request": {
    "certificateData": "$(awk '{printf "%s\\n", $0}' root-ca.pem)",
    "partnerDomain": "AUTH"
  },
  "requesttime": "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S.000Z)",
  "version": "string"
}
EOF
  echo 1>&2
  echo

  echo Run onboarding jobs
  helm -n $NS upgrade partner-onboarder mosip/partner-onboarder \
  $NFS_OPTION \
  $S3_OPTION \
  --set onboarding.variables.push_reports_to_s3=$push_reports_to_s3 \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[0]=global \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[1]=keycloak-env-vars \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[2]=keycloak-host \
  $ENABLE_INSECURE \
  -f values.yaml \
  --version $CHART_VERSION \
  --wait-for-jobs \
  --post-renderer ./post-render.sh
```

title: Partner Onboarder: Jobs fail in sandbox environment due to missing trust for corporate CA (v3)
content:
Problem description:
Similar to the issue described in #1713 the Partner Onboarder talks to Keycloak for authentication through `${mosip-api-internal-host}`. The ingress uses a certificate signed by our corporate CA. This is not known by the pods running the onboarding jobs. 

I believe that support for such environments (corporate CA, certificates not automatically trusted) is relevant for MOSIP as people need to be able to deploy and run the system in their own, internal networks, at least for development and testing. 

I have eventually been able to work around this problem. This involves patching the job manifests using `kustomize` which isn't exactly pretty (this is why having builtin support for this would be really helpful). But here we go.

**1. Create a secret from the corporate CA**

```shell
kubectl -n onboarder create secret generic corporate-ca   --from-file=corporate-ca.pem=/path/to/corp-ca.pem
```

**2. Create post-render.sh script**

Note that for more than one job the rendered manifest is syntactically invalid as the upstream PV and PVC manifests  have no `---` separators. Hence the call to `perl` in the middle.

```shell
#!/bin/bash

command -V kustomize >/dev/null || { echo "Error, 'kustomize' command is not installed on your local system." 1>&2; exit 1; }

set -euo pipefail

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Save helm output
cat > "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

echo "Patching '$tmp/rendered.yaml' which is missing the '---' between manifests it contains." 1>&2
perl -0pi -e 's/\n(apiVersion: v1\nkind: PersistentVolume\n)/\n---\n$1/g; s/\n(apiVersion: v1\nkind: PersistentVolumeClaim\n)/\n---\n$1/g' "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

# Copy kustomize files next to rendered.yaml
cp ./kustomization.yaml patch-partner-onboarder-*.yaml "$tmp/"

# Build patched output
kustomize build "$tmp"
```

**3. Create kustomization.yaml**

```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - rendered.yaml

patches:
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-digitalcard.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-digitalcard
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-ida.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-ida
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-print.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-print
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-abis.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-abis
  - path: patch-partner-onboarder-resident.yaml
    target:
      kind: Job
      name: partner-onboarder-resident
```

**4. Create patches**

```yaml
# patch-partner-onboarder-abis.yaml
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: partner-onboarder-abis
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: partner-onboarder-abis
          volumeMounts:
            - name: corporate-ca
              mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
              subPath: corporate-ca.pem
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: corporate-ca
          secret:
            secretName: corporate-ca
```

```yaml
# patch-partner-onboarder-digitalcard.yaml
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: partner-onboarder-digitalcard
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: partner-onboarder-digitalcard
          volumeMounts:
            - name: corporate-ca
              mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
              subPath: corporate-ca.pem
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: corporate-ca
          secret:
            secretName: corporate-ca
```

```yaml
# patch-partner-onboarder-ida.yaml
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: partner-onboarder-ida
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: partner-onboarder-ida
          volumeMounts:
            - name: corporate-ca
              mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
              subPath: corporate-ca.pem
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: corporate-ca
          secret:
            secretName: corporate-ca
```

```yaml
# patch-partner-onboarder-print.yaml
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: partner-onboarder-print
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: partner-onboarder-print
          volumeMounts:
            - name: corporate-ca
              mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
              subPath: corporate-ca.pem
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: corporate-ca
          secret:
            secretName: corporate-ca
```

```yaml
# patch-partner-onboarder-resident.yaml
---
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: partner-onboarder-resident
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: partner-onboarder-resident
          volumeMounts:
            - name: corporate-ca
              mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
              subPath: corporate-ca.pem
              readOnly: true
      volumes:
        - name: corporate-ca
          secret:
            secretName: corporate-ca
```

**5. Extend values.yaml**

Mount the volume with the corporate CA into the container:
```diff
--- a/deployment/v3/mosip/partner-onboarder/values.yaml
+++ b/deployment/v3/mosip/partner-onboarder/values.yaml
@@ -1,3 +1,18 @@
+extraEnvVars:
+  - name: NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS
+    value: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
+
+extraVolumes:
+  - name: corporate-ca
+    secret:
+      secretName: corporate-ca
+
+extraVolumeMounts:
+  - name: corporate-ca
+    mountPath: /etc/ssl/certs/corporate-ca.pem
+    subPath: corporate-ca.pem
+    readOnly: true
+
 onboarding:
   modules:
     - name: ida
```

**6. Necessary changes to install.sh**

In `install.sh` add the argument `--post-renderer ./post-render.sh` to the call to `helm`, like:
```
  echo Install onboarding module
  helm -n $NS install partner-onboarder mosip/partner-onboarder \
  $NFS_OPTION \
  $S3_OPTION \
  --set onboarding.variables.push_reports_to_s3=$push_reports_to_s3 \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[0]=global \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[1]=keycloak-env-vars \
  --set extraEnvVarsCM[2]=keycloak-host \
  $ENABLE_INSECURE \
  -f values.yaml \
  --version $CHART_VERSION \
  --wait-for-jobs \
  --post-renderer ./post-render.sh
```

title: Admin module not working due to missing trust for corporate CA (Keycloak TLS / JWKS / token endpoint) (v3)
content:
Problem description:
_[moved here from **[k8s-infra repository](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/issues/189)**]_

My sandbox installation uses an ingress certificate signed by our organisation's internal CA. It has turned out that the admin module has its problems when running without public certificates. 

The first obstacle is login. After having entered `globaluser` and password, this error is displayed in the browser:
```
{"id":null,"version":null,"responsetime":"2026-04-01T11:19:39.560Z","metadata":null,"response":null,"errors":[{"errorCode":"KER-MSD-500","message":"Both provided Keys cannot be null."}]}
```

The main reason seems to be that my ingress certificate presented by the external IAM URL is unknown to the JVM in which admin-service runs. Having successfully worked around this, I found that token issuer comparison was unsuccessful.

Long story short, it looks like currently MOSIP's v3 deployment is not ready for such scenarios out of the box. I really think it should be (and this should also be verified by QA), because sandbox installations using internal CAs can be assumed to be a rather common scenario.

I have eventually succeded in getting the admin UI to work. For your reference, here's what I did (and I cannot rule out some of these steps being unnecessary):

**1. Change the configuration in admin-default.properties**

```diff
diff --git a/admin-default.properties b/admin-default.properties
index 2548bc7d..2954c663 100644
--- a/admin-default.properties
+++ b/admin-default.properties
@@ -208,7 +208,7 @@ mosip.iam.module.login_flow.response_type=code
 mosip.iam.authorization_endpoint=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/auth
 mosip.iam.module.admin_realm_id=mosip
 mosip.iam.token_endpoint=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/token
-mosip.iam.certs_endpoint=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/certs
+mosip.iam.certs_endpoint=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/certs

 regproc.token.request.appid=regproc
 regproc.token.request.clientId=mosip-regproc-client
@@ -221,7 +221,8 @@ KEYBASEDTOKENAPI=${mosip.kernel.authmanager.url}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/cli
 mosip.iam.adapter.appid=admin
 mosip.iam.adapter.clientid=mosip-admin-client
 mosip.iam.adapter.clientsecret=${mosip.admin.client.secret}
-mosip.iam.adapter.issuerURL=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip
+mosip.iam.adapter.issuerURL=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip
+mosip.keycloak.issuerUrl=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip
 mosip.authmanager.client-token-endpoint=${mosip.kernel.authmanager.url}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/clientidsecretkey
 # in minutes
 mosip.iam.adapter.validate-expiry-check-rate=1440
@@ -229,6 +230,7 @@ mosip.iam.adapter.validate-expiry-check-rate=1440
 mosip.iam.adapter.renewal-before-expiry-interval=1440
 #this should be false if you don?t use this restTemplate true if you do
 mosip.iam.adapter.self-token-renewal-enable=true
+auth-token-generator.rest.issuerUrl=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip

 # LostRid
 mosip.registration.processor.lostrid.id=mosip.registration.lostrid
@@ -277,6 +279,8 @@ mosip.kernel.jsonvalidator.file-storage-uri=LOCAL

 mosip.kernel.machineid.length=5
 auth.server.admin.issuer.uri=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/
+auth.server.admin.issuer.internal.uri=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/
+auth.server.admin.issuer.domain.validate=false
 MACHINE_GET_API=${mosip.kernel.masterdata.url}/v1/masterdata/machines/mappedmachines/
 CRYPTOMANAGERDECRYPT_API=${mosip.kernel.keymanager.url}/v1/keymanager/decrypt
 CRYPTOMANAGER_DECRYPT=${mosip.kernel.keymanager.url}/v1/keymanager/decrypt

```

**2. Create file with our certificate chain**

This file will need to be made known to the admin-service JVM before it starts. We will "inject" it later:
```shell
cat my-ingress-host.cer our-corporate-ca.pem >corp-ca-chain.pem
```

**3. Patch the helm installation for an initContainer to the admin-service deployment**

Install `kustomize` on your local host:
```shell
dnf install -y kustomize
```

Create a `post-render.sh` script:
```shell
#!/bin/bash

command -V kustomize >/dev/null || { echo "Error, 'kustomize' command is not installed on your local system." 1>&2; exit 1; }

set -euo pipefail

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Save helm output
cat > "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

# Copy kustomize files next to rendered.yaml
cp ./kustomization.yaml "$tmp/kustomization.yaml"

# Build patched output
kustomize build "$tmp"
```

Create a `kustomization.yaml` file:
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - rendered.yaml

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: admin-service
    patch: |-
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: admin-service
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            volumes:
              - name: corporate-ca
                secret:
                  secretName: corporate-ca
              - name: java-truststore
                emptyDir: {}
            initContainers:
              - name: import-corporate-ca
                image: eclipse-temurin:21-jre
                command:
                  - /bin/sh
                  - -c
                  - |
                    set -e
                    cp /opt/java/openjdk/lib/security/cacerts /work/cacerts
                    keytool -importcert \
                      -alias corporate-ca \
                      -file /ca/corp-ca.crt \
                      -keystore /work/cacerts \
                      -storepass changeit \
                      -noprompt
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: corporate-ca
                    mountPath: /ca
                    readOnly: true
                  - name: java-truststore
                    mountPath: /work
            containers:
              - name: admin-service
                env:
                  - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
                    value: >-
                      -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/work/cacerts
                      -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: java-truststore
                    mountPath: /work
```

Patch `install.sh` to (a) create a `secret` from the above `.pem` file and (b) activate post-render for the `admin-service` installation:
```diff
diff --git a/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh b/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
index 9a08a24a..e450773f 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
@@ -18,6 +18,15 @@ function installing_admin() {
   kubectl label ns $NS istio-injection=enabled --overwrite
   helm repo update

+  if [ -r ../corp-ca-chain.pem ]; then
+    echo "File '../corp-ca-chain.pem' found, preparing for sandbox installation with internal CA root."
+    kubectl -n admin delete secret corporate-ca 2>/dev/null || /bin/true
+    kubectl -n admin create secret generic corporate-ca --from-file=corp-ca.crt=../corp-ca-chain.pem || errorExit "Error creating 'corporate-ca' secret."
+    ADMIN_SERVICE_HELM_POST_RENDER='--post-renderer ./post-render.sh'
+  else
+    echo "No file '../corp-ca-chain.pem' found, assuming non-sandbox install."
+  fi
+
   echo Copy configmaps
   sed -i 's/\r$//' copy_cm.sh
   ./copy_cm.sh
@@ -32,7 +41,7 @@ function installing_admin() {
   helm -n $NS install admin-hotlist mosip/admin-hotlist --version $CHART_VERSION

   echo Installing admin service. Will wait till service gets installed.
-  helm -n $NS install admin-service mosip/admin-service --set istio.corsPolicy.allowOrigins\[0\].prefix=https://$ADMIN_HOST --wait --version $CHART_VERSION
+  helm -n $NS install admin-service mosip/admin-service --set istio.corsPolicy.allowOrigins\[0\].prefix=https://$ADMIN_HOST --wait --version $CHART_VERSION $ADMIN_SERVICE_HELM_POST_RENDER

   echo Installing admin-ui
   helm -n $NS install admin-ui mosip/admin-ui --set admin.apiUrl=https://$API_HOST/v1/ --set istio.hosts\[0\]=$ADMIN_HOST --version $CHART_VERSION
```

Note that the `corp-ca-chain.pem` file is expected to reside in the `mosip-infra/deployment/v3/mosip` directory, because I assume that this problem will eventually also need to be fixed for other MOSIP modules, too.

title: Config Server renders invalid values when installed with helm chart version 1.3.0 (v3)
content:
Problem description:
I use a single remote, public git repository for the config server. My `values.yaml` looks like this:
```
activeProfileEnv: default

gitRepo:
  uri: "https://my.server/repo.git"
  version: mybranch
  searchFolders: ""
  private: false

spring_profiles:
  enabled: false

localRepo:
  enabled: false

extraEnvVars:
  - enabled: true
    name: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
    value: git

extraEnvVars:
  - name: SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE
    value: default
  - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_SERVER_GIT_URI
    value: "https://my.server/repo.git"
  - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_SERVER_GIT_DEFAULT_LABEL
    value: "mybranch"
  - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_SERVER_GIT_CLONE_ON_START
    value: "true"
  - name: SPRING_CLOUD_CONFIG_SERVER_GIT_FORCE_PULL
    value: "true"
```

After installation the configmap `config-server-share` contains placeholders for the branch name:
```
kubectl -n config-server get configmap config-server-share -o yaml

apiVersion: v1
data:
  active_profile_env: git
  cache_config_url_env: http://config-server.config-server/config/application/git/<
    branch-name >/hazelcast_cache.xml
  consolidator_config_file_url_env: http://config-server.config-server/config/application/git/<
    branch-name >/websub-consolidator.toml
  hub_config_file_url_env: http://config-server.config-server/config/application/git/<
    branch-name >/websub-service.toml
  spring_config_label_env: < branch-name >
  spring_config_url_env: http://config-server.config-server/config
kind: ConfigMap
metadata:
  annotations:
    meta.helm.sh/release-name: config-server
    meta.helm.sh/release-namespace: config-server
  creationTimestamp: "2026-03-17T18:43:15Z"
  labels:
    app.kubernetes.io/managed-by: Helm
  name: config-server-share
  namespace: config-server
  resourceVersion: "210306"
  uid: 59e7f637-eb7d-4338-9fbc-8e9cf75ea546
```

After some digging it has turned out that this problem can be fixed by switching to a more recent version of the helm chart in `install.sh`:
```
CHART_VERSION=12.0.3
```

title: Installation / execution of config server fails (v3)
content:
Problem description:
With recent changes from 2025 config server installation stopped working.

First issue: missing configmap `postgres-setup-config`. I have found it mentioned somewhere in the repo, but it is not created automatically anywhere. Creating it manually seems to work:
```
    kubectl -n config-server create configmap postgres-setup-config \
      --from-literal=mosip-database-hostname-override=postgres-postgresql.postgres \
      --from-literal=mosip-database-port-override=5432
```

Also as of now it looks like "composite" spring profile for configuring the git repo(s) containing the configuration cannot easily be overridden to use a single remote git repo. The following settings in `values.yaml` used to work:
```

  uri: "https://github.com/mosip/mosip-config.git"
  version: release-1.3.x
  ## Folders within the base repo where properties may be found.
  searchFolders: ""
  private: false
  ## User name of user who has access to the private repo. Ignore for public repo
  username: ""
  token: ""
```

This is however no longer the case. Now I need to override defaults using the environment, which does not seem right:
```
activeProfileEnv: default

gitRepo:
  uri: "https://my.server/repo.git"
  version: mybranch
  searchFolders: ""
  private: false
```

title: ActiveMQ CrashLoop because of startupProbe being too strict (v3)
content:
Problem description:
In thre provided ActiveMQ installation the `startupProbe` is too strict (netcat 61616) causing `CrashLoopBackOff` on slow storage/VMs; needs configurable probes or higher thresholds.

Current workaround:
```
diff --git a/deployment/v3/external/activemq/install.sh b/deployment/v3/external/activemq/install.sh
index e7c331cd..4bf5430d 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/external/activemq/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/external/activemq/install.sh
@@ -20,7 +20,7 @@ function installing_Activemq() {
   echo Installing Activemq
   ACTIVEMQ_HOST=$(kubectl get cm global -o jsonpath={.data.mosip-activemq-host})
   echo Activemq host: $ACTIVEMQ_HOST
-  helm -n $NS install activemq mosip/activemq-artemis -f values.yaml --set istio.hosts[0]="$ACTIVEMQ_HOST" --wait
+  helm -n $NS install activemq mosip/activemq-artemis -f values.yaml --set istio.hosts[0]="$ACTIVEMQ_HOST" --post-renderer ./post-render.sh --wait
   return 0
 }
```

post-render.sh:
```
#!/bin/sh

command -V kustomize >/dev/null || { echo "Error, 'kustomize' command is not installed on your local system." 1>&2; exit 1; }

set -euo pipefail

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Save helm output
cat > "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

# Copy kustomize files next to rendered.yaml
cp ./kustomization.yaml "$tmp/kustomization.yaml"

# Build patched output
kustomize build "$tmp"
```

kustomization.yaml:
```
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization
namespace: activemq

resources:
  - rendered.yaml

patches:
  - target:
      group: apps
      version: v1
      kind: StatefulSet
      name: activemq-activemq-artemis-slave
    patch: |-
      - op: replace
        path: /spec/template/spec/containers/0/startupProbe
        value:
          httpGet:
            path: /
            port: 8161
          initialDelaySeconds: 30
          periodSeconds: 10
          timeoutSeconds: 5
          failureThreshold: 12
```

title: MinIO installation fails due to unresolvable images (v3)
content:
Problem description:
bitnami has moved the image referenced in the repo away, so that mosip-infra/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh fails:

- The `minio` image needs to be pulled from the legacy repo. The exact image is not available there, but the same version with a slightly different tag.
- The `minio-console` image seems to have completely disappeared. Hence it must be disabled (as it does not seem to be necessary for running MinIO).
- In that configuration with an NFS-based PV I found that the corresponding PVC was ignored so that the container failed when trying to write to the readonly-mounted cotainer FS. I needed extra settings for the helm chart in order to enforce using the PVC.

The following change works for me:
```
diff --git a/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh b/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh
index bf3f677e..dee12fdc 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/external/object-store/minio/install.sh
@@ -14,7 +14,14 @@ kubectl label ns $NS istio-injection=enabled --overwrite

 function installing_minio() {
   echo Installing minio
-  helm -n minio install minio mosip/minio --version 10.1.6
+  helm upgrade --install minio bitnami/minio -n minio \
+    --set image.repository=bitnamilegacy/minio \
+    --set image.tag=2022.2.7 \
+    --set console.enabled=false \
+    --set persistence.mountPath=/data \
+    --set extraVolumeMounts[0].name=empty-dir \
+    --set extraVolumeMounts[0].mountPath=/.minio \
+    --set extraVolumeMounts[0].subPath=dot-minio

   echo Installing gateways and virtualservice
   EXTERNAL_HOST=$(kubectl get cm global -o jsonpath={.data.mosip-minio-host})
```

Discussion and resolution:
[mbert]: With the changes from December 2 and December 24 the installation still does not work:
```
Create minio namespace
namespace/minio created
namespace/minio labeled
```

title: Installation of Istio gateway (Keycloak install.sh) fails due to missing configmap 'global' (v3)
content:
Problem description:
After the recent refactoring of the install documentation the section on the configmap `global` and related information about what it is good for, how to create it correctly etc. was removed ([global_configmap.yml.sample](https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/blob/master/main/README.md) no longer exists).

However installation still depends on it: [Keycloak install.sh](https://github.com/mosip/mosip-infra/blob/master/deployment/v3/external/iam/install.sh) will fail if the configmap has not been installed.

Also in various files dead links to it exist.

title: Keycloak installation fails due to unresolvable image
content:
Problem description:
bitnami has moved the image referenced in the repo away, so that mosip-infra/deployment/v3/external/iam/install.sh fails. The following change works for me:
```
diff --git a/deployment/v3/external/iam/install.sh b/deployment/v3/external/iam/install.sh
index 0f1a7dda..74a62bb4 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/external/iam/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/external/iam/install.sh
@@ -19,7 +19,18 @@ function installing_keycloak() {
   helm repo update
 
   echo Installing
-  helm -n $NS install $SERVICE_NAME mosip/keycloak --version "7.1.18" --set image.repository=mosipid/mosip-artemis-keycloak --set image.tag=1.2.0.1 --set image.pullPolicy=Always -f values.yaml --wait
+  helm -n "$NS" upgrade --install keycloak mosip/keycloak \
+  --version "7.1.18" -f values.yaml \
+  --set image.registry=docker.io \
+  --set image.repository="mosipqa/mosip-artemis-keycloak@sha256" \
+  --set image.tag="ad525bb1e81531701aab754c8a090b887c4f97ca642cc348dc1de59cae649dcc" \
+  --set postgresql.enabled=true \
+  --set postgresql.image.registry=docker.io \
+  --set postgresql.image.repository=bitnamilegacy/postgresql \
+  --set postgresql.image.tag="14.12.0-debian-12-r22" \
+  --set image.pullPolicy=Always \
+  --wait
+
 
   EXTERNAL_HOST=$(kubectl get cm global -o jsonpath={.data.mosip-iam-external-host})
   echo Install Istio gateway, virtual service

```

Discussion and resolution:
[vv0rk0ffice]: try this PR where is replaced bitnami with bitnamilegacy 

https://github.com/mosip/mosip-infra/pull/1668

[mbert]: Seems to be fixed now by recent commits.

content:
Problem description:
bitnami has moved the image referenced in the repo away, so that `mosip-infra/deployment/v3/external/postgres/install.sh` fails. The following change works for me:

```
diff --git a/deployment/v3/external/postgres/install.sh b/deployment/v3/external/postgres/install.sh
index 960578d0..3fef24e5 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/external/postgres/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/external/postgres/install.sh
@@ -15,7 +15,7 @@ kubectl label ns $NS istio-injection=enabled --overwrite
 
 function installing_postgres() {
   echo Installing  Postgres
-  helm -n $NS install postgres bitnami/postgresql --version 12.11.1 -f values.yaml --wait
+  helm -n $NS install postgres bitnami/postgresql --version 12.11.1 -f values.yaml --set image.registry=docker.io --set image.repository=bitnamilegacy/postgresql --set image.tag=15.4.0-debian-11-r10 --wait
   echo Installed Postgres
 
   echo Installing gateways and virtual services
```

Discussion and resolution:
[mbert]: Seems to be fixed now by recent commits.
