title: [DMP 2026]:  Enhancement: Track Supervisor ID in Registration Packet Processing
content:
Problem description: ### Ticket Contents ## Description User Story Statement: As a country representative, I want to capture supervisor details during packet approval/rejection, so that I can generate reports mapping supervisors to approved/rejected packets. As-Is: Currently, when a supervisor approves or rejects a registration packet, the system captures details such as status (Approved/Rejected), comments, and timestamp. However, the supervisor ID is not captured, making it difficult to track which supervisor performed the action for reporting purposes. To-Be: The system should capture and persist the supervisor ID along with approval/rejection details during packet processing. This will enable traceability and reporting (supervisor vs approved/rejected packets). Additionally, supervisor validation should be enforced during processing, and packets uploaded via admin and supervisors should be distinguished and tracked separately. ### Goals & Mid-Point Milestone: ## Goals: - [ ] Capture supervisor ID during packet approval/rejection - [ ] Enable reporting based on supervisor vs packet status - [ ] Enforce supervisor validation during processing stage - [ ] Differentiate and track admin-uploaded vs supervisor-uploaded packets [Goals Achieved By Mid-point Milestone] - [ ] Sync V3 API updated to include supervisorId - [ ] Registration client sends supervisorId during sync - [ ] Basic persistence of supervisorId in DB - [ ] Initial validation logic implemented ### Setup/Installation: This feature will be implemented as part of the Registration Client. Please refer to the [developer guide](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-processor/develop/registration-processor-developers-guide) for further details. ### Expected Outcome: - Supervisor ID is captured and stored for every approval/rejection - Reporting systems can use supervisorId for analytics - Supervisor validation is enforced during processing - Admin-uploaded packets are tracked separately - Backward compatibility is maintained for older packets ### Acceptance Criteria - Supervisor must be onboarded and mapped to center - Supervisor must be able to login and approve/reject packets - Supervisor must be able to enter comments - On approval/rejection: - Supervisor ID, status, comment, and timestamp must be stored - Supervisor validation must be performed during processing stage - Admin-uploaded packets must: - Capture admin ID as supervisorId - Be marked and tracked separately - Supervisor-uploaded packets must undergo validation - System must support backward compatibility (nullable supervisorId) - Sync V3 API must accept and validate supervisorId

Alternate Scenarios

Scenario ID Scenario Condition System Behavior User/System Message
AS-01 Supervisor Approval Supervisor approves packet Capture supervisorId, status, comment, timestamp Packet approved successfully.
AS-02 Supervisor Rejection Supervisor rejects packet Capture supervisorId, status, comment, timestamp Packet rejected successfully.
AS-03 Admin Upload Approval Admin uploads approved packet Capture adminId as supervisorId with other fields status, comment, timestamp Packet uploaded and approved by admin.
AS-04 Admin Upload Rejection Admin uploads rejected packet Capture adminId as supervisorId with other fields status, comment, timestamp Packet uploaded and rejected by admin.
AS-05 Backward Compatibility Flow Older packet without supervisorId Allow processing with conditional validation Processing packet with legacy data.

Error Scenarios

Scenario Condition System Behavior Error Message
Missing Supervisor ID SupervisorId not present in sync request Block processing for V3 API Supervisor ID is required for processing.
Mismatch Supervisor ID SupervisorId in packet and sync do not match Throw validation error Supervisor ID mismatch detected. Validation failed.
Supervisor Validation Failure Supervisor validation fails during processing Reject packet at validation stage Supervisor validation failed.
Admin Packet Validation Skipped Incorrectly Admin packet incorrectly sent for validation Skip validation and log warning Admin packet validation skipped.
Database Persistence Failure Failure while storing supervisorId Abort transaction Error saving supervisor details. Please retry.
API Validation Error Invalid request in Sync V3 Reject request Invalid sync request. Please verify input.
Legacy Packet Handling Error Old packet with missing data and config mismatch Fail validation based on config rules Legacy packet validation failed.
Reporting Data Inconsistency SupervisorId missing in DB for reporting Log error and flag record Supervisor data missing for reporting.
### Implementation Details

Overview

This enhancement introduces a new Sync V3 API in the Registration Processor to capture the supervisorId as part of the sync registration request. The captured supervisorId will be stored in the database and used for reporting (supervisor vs approved/rejected packets) and traceability.

Assumptions

  • Supervisor authentication (biometric/password) is performed locally in the Registration Client before sending the sync request
  • Only authenticated supervisors can initiate packet approval/rejection
  • Admin portal uploads do not require biometric authentication
  • Admin users can upload packets with approval/rejection remarks
  • Admin login ID will be treated as supervisorId for admin-uploaded packets

Key Clarifications

  • supervisorId will be stored in DB for reporting visibility
  • supervisorId will be nullable to support backward compatibility
  • If supervisorId exists in both:
    • Packet metadata and sync request → both must match
    • Else → validation error

API Changes

New Endpoint

/registrationprocessor/v1/registrationstatus/syncV3

Database Changes

Table Name | Column Name | Data Type | Constraint -- | -- | -- | -- registration_list | supervisor_id | character varying | nullable

Validation Decision Tree

START

IF Sync V3:
    IF Admin Upload:
        - Use adminId as supervisorId
        - Skip validation
        - Mark as admin-uploaded
        - Proceed

    IF supervisorId is NULL:
        - Allow (Backward compatibility)
        - Proceed

    IF supervisorId present in packet:
        IF mismatch with sync supervisorId:
            ❌ ERROR: Supervisor ID mismatch → STOP

    Perform Supervisor Validation:
        IF authentication failed:
            ❌ ERROR → STOP

        IF not mapped to center:
            ❌ ERROR → STOP

        ✅ SUCCESS → Proceed

ELSE (Sync V2 / Legacy):
    IF Reg Client version configured:
        IF supervisorId present in packet:
            → Validate
        ELSE:
            → Proceed
    ELSE:
        → Proceed

END

Processing Logic

  • Capture supervisorId from:
    • Registration Client (Supervisor flow)
    • Admin Portal (Admin login ID)
  • Store supervisorId in DB
  • Validate supervisor during processing stage
  • Skip validation for admin-uploaded packets
  • Track admin-uploaded packets separately

Backward Compatibility

  • Sync V2 continues without supervisorId
  • Sync V3 supports optional supervisorId
  • Existing records without supervisorId remain valid
  • Validation behavior depends on:
    • Client version
    • Configuration

Error Handling

  • Supervisor ID mismatch → validation failure
  • Missing supervisorId (V3) → allowed (backward compatibility)
  • Invalid supervisor → reject during validation stage
  • Unauthorized supervisor → reject
  • DB failure → abort transaction

title: [DMP 2026]: Enhancement: Track Supervisor ID in Registration Packet Processing
content:
Problem description: ### Ticket Contents ## Description **User Story Statement:** As a country representative, I want to capture supervisor details during packet approval/rejection, so that I can generate reports mapping supervisors to approved/rejected packets. **As-Is:** Currently, when a supervisor approves or rejects a registration packet, the system captures details such as status (Approved/Rejected), comments, and timestamp. However, the supervisor ID is not captured, making it difficult to track which supervisor performed the action for reporting purposes. **To-Be:** The system should capture and persist the supervisor ID along with approval/rejection details during packet processing. This will enable traceability and reporting (supervisor vs approved/rejected packets). Additionally, supervisor validation should be enforced during processing, and packets uploaded via admin and supervisors should be distinguished and tracked separately. ### Goals & Mid-Point Milestone ## Goals - Capture supervisor ID during packet approval/rejection - Enable reporting based on supervisor vs packet status - Enforce supervisor validation during processing stage - Differentiate and track admin-uploaded vs supervisor-uploaded packets ### Goals Achieved By Mid-point Milestone - Sync V3 API updated to include supervisorId - Registration client sends supervisorId during sync - Basic persistence of supervisorId in DB - Initial validation logic implemented ### Setup/Installation This feature will be implemented as part of the Registration Client. Please refer to the [developer guide](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-processor/develop/registration-processor-developers-guide) for further details. ### Expected Outcome - Supervisor ID is captured and stored for every approval/rejection - Reporting systems can use supervisorId for analytics - Supervisor validation is enforced during processing - Admin-uploaded packets are tracked separately - Backward compatibility is maintained for older packets ### Acceptance Criteria **Acceptance Criteria** - Supervisor must be onboarded and mapped to center - Supervisor must be able to login and approve/reject packets - Supervisor must be able to enter comments - On approval/rejection: - Supervisor ID, status, comment, and timestamp must be stored - Supervisor validation must be performed during processing stage - Admin-uploaded packets must: - Capture admin ID as supervisorId - Be marked and tracked separately - Supervisor-uploaded packets must undergo validation - System must support backward compatibility (nullable supervisorId) - Sync V3 API must accept and validate supervisorId

Alternate Scenarios

Scenario ID Scenario Condition System Behavior User/System Message
AS-01 Supervisor Approval Supervisor approves packet Capture supervisorId, status, comment, timestamp Packet approved successfully.
AS-02 Supervisor Rejection Supervisor rejects packet Capture supervisorId, status, comment, timestamp Packet rejected successfully.
AS-03 Admin Upload Approval Admin uploads approved packet Capture adminId as supervisorId with other fields status, comment, timestamp Packet uploaded and approved by admin.
AS-04 Admin Upload Rejection Admin uploads rejected packet Capture adminId as supervisorId with other fields status, comment, timestamp Packet uploaded and rejected by admin.
AS-05 Backward Compatibility Flow Older packet without supervisorId Allow processing with conditional validation Processing packet with legacy data.

Error Scenarios

Scenario Condition System Behavior Error Message
Missing Supervisor ID SupervisorId not present in sync request Block processing for V3 API Supervisor ID is required for processing.
Mismatch Supervisor ID SupervisorId in packet and sync do not match Throw validation error Supervisor ID mismatch detected. Validation failed.
Supervisor Validation Failure Supervisor validation fails during processing Reject packet at validation stage Supervisor validation failed.
Admin Packet Validation Skipped Incorrectly Admin packet incorrectly sent for validation Skip validation and log warning Admin packet validation skipped.
Database Persistence Failure Failure while storing supervisorId Abort transaction Error saving supervisor details. Please retry.
API Validation Error Invalid request in Sync V3 Reject request Invalid sync request. Please verify input.
Legacy Packet Handling Error Old packet with missing data and config mismatch Fail validation based on config rules Legacy packet validation failed.
Reporting Data Inconsistency SupervisorId missing in DB for reporting Log error and flag record Supervisor data missing for reporting.
### Implementation Details

Overview

This enhancement introduces a new Sync V3 API in the Registration Processor to capture the supervisorId as part of the sync registration request. The captured supervisorId will be stored in the database and used for reporting (supervisor vs approved/rejected packets) and traceability.

Assumptions

  • Supervisor authentication (biometric/password) is performed locally in the Registration Client before sending the sync request
  • Only authenticated supervisors can initiate packet approval/rejection
  • Admin portal uploads do not require biometric authentication
  • Admin users can upload packets with approval/rejection remarks
  • Admin login ID will be treated as supervisorId for admin-uploaded packets

Key Clarifications

  • supervisorId will be stored in DB for reporting visibility
  • supervisorId will be nullable to support backward compatibility
  • If supervisorId exists in both:
    • Packet metadata and sync request → both must match
    • Else → validation error

API Changes

New Endpoint

/registrationprocessor/v1/registrationstatus/syncV3

Database Changes

Table Name Column Name Data Type Constraint
registration_list supervisor_id character varying nullable

Validation Decision Tree

START

IF Sync V3:
    IF Admin Upload:
        - Use adminId as supervisorId
        - Skip validation
        - Mark as admin-uploaded
        - Proceed

    IF supervisorId is NULL:
        - Allow (Backward compatibility)
        - Proceed

    IF supervisorId present in packet:
        IF mismatch with sync supervisorId:
            ❌ ERROR: Supervisor ID mismatch → STOP

    Perform Supervisor Validation:
        IF authentication failed:
            ❌ ERROR → STOP

        IF not mapped to center:
            ❌ ERROR → STOP

        ✅ SUCCESS → Proceed

ELSE (Sync V2 / Legacy):
    IF Reg Client version configured:
        IF supervisorId present in packet:
            → Validate
        ELSE:
            → Proceed
    ELSE:
        → Proceed

END

Processing Logic

  • Capture supervisorId from:
    • Registration Client (Supervisor flow)
    • Admin Portal (Admin login ID)
  • Store supervisorId in DB
  • Validate supervisor during processing stage
  • Skip validation for admin-uploaded packets
  • Track admin-uploaded packets separately

Backward Compatibility

  • Sync V2 continues without supervisorId
  • Sync V3 supports optional supervisorId
  • Existing records without supervisorId remain valid
  • Validation behavior depends on:
    • Client version
    • Configuration

Error Handling

  • Supervisor ID mismatch → validation failure
  • Missing supervisorId (V3) → allowed (backward compatibility)
  • Invalid supervisor → reject during validation stage
  • Unauthorized supervisor → reject

title: Draft API Integration – Creation of New Stage Before Quality Classifier
content:
Problem description:

Title:

Enhance the Draft API Implementation by Introducing a New "Create Draft" Stage Before the Quality Classifier Stage

Description:

As a developer, I want to introduce a new “Create Draft” stage in the registration processing pipeline, placed before the Quality Classifier stage, so that the Draft API is created and updated earlier in the workflow. This change replaces the current dependency on the Packet Manager for demographic and biometric data retrieval, improves modularity, and aligns with the updated ID Repository workflow.

The new stage will handle Draft API creation and updates for NEW and UPDATE packets, ensuring data consistency and improving performance during downstream stage processing.

Acceptance Criteria

1. Create Draft API – New Stage Integration

  • A new stage called “create_draft” must be introduced in the registration processor workflow.

  • The create_draft stage should be positioned before the Quality Classifier stage for both NEW and UPDATEpackets.

  • The stage will handle the creation and updating of the Draft for each packet, containing both demographic and biometric data (excluding evidence files).

  • UIN allocation is mandatory during Draft creation.

  • If a Draft already exists for a given RID, it should be deleted and re-created.

  • Drafts must be discarded if the packet processing fails or is rejected.

  • In case of a reprocess, the Draft must remain active until the packet processing completes.

  • Once the UIN is successfully generated, the Draft must be published and then discarded.

2. Replacement of Packet Manager Calls

  • Post create_draft stage, subsequent stages like Demo Dedup, Bio Dedup, ABIS Handler, Manual Adjudication, and Verification must use the Draft API instead of the Packet Manager for data retrieval.

  • The Draft API must provide granular retrieval options:

    • Retrieve demographics only

    • Retrieve biometrics only

    • Retrieve both, when no filter is applied (default behavior)

  • Evidence files are not part of the Draft data.

3. Quality Classifier Stage Alignment

  • The new create_draft stage should seamlessly pass validated data to the Quality Classifier stage.

  • The Quality Classifier will not be modified functionally but must consume data from the newly created Draft rather than the packet manager.

4. UIN Generator Stage Update

  • The UIN Generator stage will no longer create Drafts for NEW or UPDATE packets.

  • It will only handle Draft creation for Lost Packets after ABIS stages, as per existing logic.

  • On successful UIN generation, the corresponding Draft must be updated and published to the ID Repository, after which it is discarded.

5. Validation and Error Handling

  • Implement strong validation rules for Draft creation to ensure a unique draft per RID.

  • Proper error handling must be added for transition failures between stages.

  • Draft API operations must not alter existing business rules except for the new stage insertion and timing of Draft creation.

6. Backward Compatibility

  • Maintain backward compatibility for existing UIN Generator workflows.

  • Default retrieval behavior must remain unchanged when no type parameter is specified.

Use Cases

Use Case #1: New Registration

Basic Flow

  1. A resident submits a new registration packet.

  2. The packet passes all validation stages up to the Quality Classifier.

  3. Before entering Quality Classifier, the create_draft stage triggers Draft creation using the Draft API.

    • Draft is tagged as “New” and stores demographics and biometrics (no evidence data).

  4. Subsequent stages (Demo Dedup, Bio Dedup, etc.) retrieve required data via Draft API.

  5. Once UIN is generated, the Draft is updated and published to the ID Repository.

  6. After publishing, the Draft is discarded.

Alternate Flow #1:
If the packet fails or is rejected, the corresponding Draft must be deleted immediately.

Alternate Flow #2:
If the packet is marked for reprocessing, the Draft must remain active until completion.

Use Case #2: Update Registration

Basic Flow

  1. A resident with an existing UIN updates their demographic or biometric details.

  2. The packet passes validation up to the Quality Classifier.

  3. Before entering Quality Classifier, the create_draft stage creates/updates the Draft API tagged as “Update”.

  4. Downstream stages retrieve data from the Draft API instead of Packet Manager.

  5. After UIN regeneration, the updated UIN is stored in the Draft, which is then published and discarded.

Alternate Flow #1:
If the packet fails or is rejected, the corresponding Draft must be deleted.

Alternate Flow #2:
If the packet is marked for reprocessing, the Draft must remain until successful completion.

Technical Implementation Overview (from Impact Analysis v1.3)

High-Level Summary

The Draft API replaces Packet Manager calls from the Demo Dedup stage onward.
Changes include:

  • Addition of a new “create_draft” stage before the Quality Classifier.

  • Enhancements to Draft API for granular retrieval (demographics, biometrics, or both).

  • Updates to affected stages to consume data from the Draft API.

  • UIN Generator stage refactoring to remove Draft creation logic for NEW/UPDATE packets.

Component-Level Impacts

Component | Change Summary -- | -- Draft API | Add query parameter-based retrieval (type=demographics, type=biometrics). New Stage (create_draft) | Create/Update Drafts for NEW & UPDATE packets, before Quality Classifier. Demo Dedup / Bio Dedup / ABIS / Verification / Manual Adjudication | Replace Packet Manager reads with Draft API calls. UIN Generator | Remove Draft creation logic for NEW/UPDATE packets; retain only for lost packets. Packet Classifier | Add handling for anonymous tag file creation and object store storage. Work Manager | Update to use enriched getTags API to retrieve anonymous data instead of Packet Manager.

Definition of Done

  • New create_draft stage implemented and placed before Quality Classifier.

  • Draft API enhanced to support granular data retrieval.

  • All dependent stages refactored to use Draft API instead of Packet Manager.

  • UIN Generator logic updated as per new design.

  • Backward compatibility verified.

  • All unit, integration, and regression tests successfully executed.

title: Add application/json Content-Type to requests
content:
Problem description:
For device request() and fetch() calls that include a JSON body in the request, it would be better to explicitly add a Content-Type of 'application/json' to the headers so that client libraries can automatically validate the request for properly formed JSON.    Otherwise browsers such as Chrome or Edge send the request as text/plain.

title: [DMP 2026]: Define Biometric Quality Through SDK During Biometric Capture
content:
Problem description: ### Ticket Contents ## Description **User Story:** As a registration system, I want the registration client to support SDK-based biometric quality evaluation with SBI fallback, so that biometric capture quality is validated in real time. **As-Is:** Currently, the registration client validates biometric quality using the SBI-provided quality score, and the score is compared against the existing configurable biometric quality threshold defined in the system configuration. **To-Be:** The registration client should support evaluating biometric quality using an SDK during biometric capture, while continuing to use the existing configuration-based threshold validation mechanism. The SDK-generated score will be validated against the same threshold currently used for SBI. If the SDK is unavailable or fails, the system will fall back to SBI quality scores. ### Goals & Mid-Point Milestone **Goals** - Enable SDK-based biometric quality evaluation during capture - Reuse the existing biometric quality threshold configuration without modification - Provide real-time feedback to operators for biometric quality validation - Ensure seamless fallback to SBI quality scores when SDK is unavailable or fails **Goals Achieved By Mid-point Milestone** - SDK integration framework enabled in the registration client - Ability to fetch and process SDK-based quality scores - Initial validation of SDK scores against existing thresholds - Basic fallback mechanism to SBI implemented ### Setup/Installation This feature has to be implemented as part of the Registration Client. Please refer to the [developer guide](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-client/develop/registration-client-developers-guide) for further details. ### Expected Outcome - Biometric quality is evaluated in real time using SDK where available - Existing threshold validation mechanism continues unchanged - Operators are prompted to re-capture biometrics when quality is below threshold - System falls back to SBI scoring seamlessly without disrupting the flow - Registration is blocked if no valid quality score is available ### Acceptance Criteria - Registration client supports SDK-based biometric quality evaluation - SDK-generated scores are validated against existing configurable thresholds - SBI fallback is triggered when SDK is unavailable, disabled, or fails - Re-capture is enforced when quality scores fall below threshold - System handles error scenarios including invalid SDK responses, timeouts, and partial captures - Registration is blocked when both SDK and SBI scores are unavailable - All quality evaluations, fallbacks, and errors are logged for audit purposes

Alternate Scenarios

Scenario ID Scenario Condition System Behavior User/System Message
AS-01 SDK-based Quality Evaluation SDK available and valid SDK score used against existing threshold Biometric quality captured successfully.
AS-02 SBI Fallback SDK unavailable SBI score used against existing threshold Using system default quality score for validation.
AS-03 SDK Disabled SDK turned off in configuration SBI quality validation continues SDK-based quality evaluation is disabled. Using default scoring.
AS-04 Re-capture Flow Quality below threshold Re-capture enforced Captured biometric quality is below acceptable threshold. Please re-capture.

Error Scenarios

Scenario Condition System Behavior Error Message
Invalid SDK Score SDK configured, returns null / invalid value Display error, block registration, and prompt operator to re-capture biometrics. No fallback to SBI. Invalid biometric quality score received from SDK.
SDK Timeout SDK configured, response delayed Display error, block progression, and prompt re-capture. No fallback to SBI. Biometric quality evaluation timed out. Please re-capture biometrics.
SDK Exception SDK configured, runtime/integration error Display error, block registration, and prompt re-capture. No fallback to SBI. Error occurred during SDK-based quality evaluation. Please retry capture.
Missing SBI Score SBI configured as quality source but no score returned Block registration and prompt re-capture or retry. Default biometric quality score unavailable.
No Quality Source Neither SDK nor SBI configured Block registration and prevent further processing. Biometric quality evaluation is not configured. Registration cannot proceed.
Quality Below Threshold Score (SDK or SBI) below threshold Enforce re-capture of biometrics before proceeding. Biometric quality below acceptable threshold. Please re-capture.
Partial Capture Missing required biometric modality Block progression and prompt completion of all required biometric captures. Incomplete biometric capture. Please capture all required biometrics.
Corrupt Data Invalid or unreadable biometric data Reject captured data and prompt re-capture. Captured biometric data is invalid. Please re-capture.
Configuration Error Invalid or missing threshold/config setup Block process and notify administrator. Biometric quality configuration error. Please contact administrator.
Audit Log Failure Logging failure Allow process to continue but log warning for audit purposes. Warning: Unable to record biometric quality audit details.
**Out of scope** - Multiple SDK integration is not supported. ### Implementation Details TBA ### Mockups/Wireframes Not Applicable ### Product Name MOSIP ### Organisation Name MOSIP ### Domain Open Source Project ### Tech Skills Needed Java ### Mentor(s) @Varaniya @JanardhanBS-SyncByte @anushasunkada ### Category Backend Discussion and resolution: [aniket866]: hi @Varaniya201 I would like to work on this Please feel free to assign [Pragya279]: Hi @aniket866 Thank you for your interest in contributing. It’s great to see your enthusiasm. The DMP tickets are specifically intended for interns who participated in MOSIP Decode, which was one of our student hackathons. That said, we truly appreciate your interest in contributing. Please stay tuned! We will soon be publishing a list of GitHub issues that are open for the broader community to contribute to. Looking forward to your participation! [bhanuprabhas]: Adding this issue to the C4GT-Badal [sanyabakshi18]: Hello team! I would like to contribute to this project Please help me know how to proceed and feel free to assign work. [irnahura]: Hi @Varaniya @JanardhanBS-SyncByte @anushasunkada, I'd like to take this up — and I think I'm in a strong position to deliver it well. I've worked on biometric capture and validation pipelines during my internship, including real-time score evaluation, threshold-based gating, and fallback logic — which is essentially the core of what this issue asks for. Java backend work is comfortable territory for me, and I've dealt with SDK integration patterns, timeout handling, and audit logging in production-grade systems before. I've already gone through the Registration Client codebase. Beyond this ticket, I spotted a few other areas worth flagging (I'll open separate issues for those). That exploration also gave me a solid enough understanding of the existing SBI quality flow to know exactly where the SDK evaluation layer needs to plug in. Here's my approach for this feature: - Introduce an SDK quality evaluator as a pluggable component that sits above the existing SBI flow, keeping the threshold config completely untouched - SBI fallback only triggers when SDK is absent or disabled in config — not on runtime errors (per the error scenarios), which needs careful conditional branching - Timeout and exception handling will be isolated so SDK failures are loud and auditable but never silently degrade to SBI - The fallback and evaluation decisions will be fully logged for the audit trail I've thought this through end to end and I'm ready to start. Would be great to work with the team on this! [keerthi01228]: Hi @Varaniya201 @JanardhanBS-SyncByte @anushasunkada, I would like to contribute to the code. Please feel free to assign the work. [Hendrixx-RE]: @bhanuprabhas Just a quick question,is this issue available for the broader public or just MOSIP Decode interns?? [bhanuprabhas]: To all the public [Hendrixx-RE]: @bhanuprabhas Submitted my proposal in the DMP portal.Kindly review it. [Kanika0306]: Hi @Varaniya201 @JanardhanBS-SyncByte @anushasunkada I'd like to take up this issue. I've gone through the registration-client codebase in detail before writing this, so let me share what I've understood and how I'd approach it. **What I've gathered from the codebase** The current biometric quality check flow is driven by the SBI (Secure Biometric Interface) layer. It captures the modality, gets a quality score back, and gates the capture based on configured thresholds in the `registration-default.properties`. The SDK quality evaluator needs to sit above this as an independent evaluation step, not a fork of the SBI path. The two should coexist with SDK taking priority when present and enabled, and SBI acting as the fallback only when SDK is explicitly absent from config and not when it throws an error at runtime. **How I'd implement it** The core of my approach would be introducing a `BiometricQualityEvaluator` interface that abstracts the evaluation contract, with two implementations, one wrapping the SDK call and one delegating to the existing SBI scorer. A config-driven resolver would decide which gets invoked at startup, keeping the rest of the capture flow completely unaware of which evaluator is active. For the SDK integration specifically, the SDK call would be wrapped in a timeout-bounded executor so a hanging SDK never blocks the capture thread. Runtime exceptions and timeout breaches would be caught, logged with full context (modality, attempt number, exception type), and surfaced as a named error code rather than silently falling back to SBI since silent degradation here would be a compliance risk. The fallback to SBI only happens when the evaluator resolver at startup determines SDK is not configured, that decision is made once and not per-capture. **On audit logging** Given that this sits in a biometric pipeline for identity registration, every evaluation decision needs to be traceable. I'd log the evaluator used, the score returned, the threshold it was compared against, and the pass/fail outcome, structured enough that it can be queried later if a registration is disputed. **On the config side** I'd keep it minimal with a single flag like `mosip.biometric.sdk.quality.enabled` and an optional timeout value, with no restructuring of the existing threshold properties. I've also traced how the quality outcome feeds into the packet builder downstream, so I'm confident the changes stay contained within the capture module without touching the packet structure. Ready to write up a formal proposal and start right away. Would love to be assigned and work closely with the team on this! [Hendrixx-RE]: @bhanuprabhas Made a PR addressing a demo MVP to the issue at hand.Kindly review the submission [Kadam-Atharva]: @Varaniya @JanardhanBS-SyncByte @anushasunkada I am highly interested in taking up this issue to implement the SDK-based biometric quality evaluation and its robust SBI fallback mechanism. With my strong background in Java and backend engineering, I am well-prepared to handle the score validation and edge cases outlined in the requirements. I am excited about the opportunity to contribute to MOSIP and looking forward to participating in C4GT DMP 2026! [KrishnaParihar1]: Hello @Varaniya201 , I’m interested in contributing to this enhancement. My approach is to build an SDK-first biometric quality validation flow in Java that reuses existing threshold settings and falls back to SBI when needed. I’d prioritize reliable error handling, enforced re-capture, and audit logging while preserving the current registration workflow. [Jayesh-git10]: Hello @Varaniya201 , I would love to work on this issue as a participant of the C4GT DMP 2026 program by adding a layer for SDK-based biometric quality evaluation in the Registration Client while keeping the existing SBI-based validation flow intact. ### Proposed Solution * Develop a common Quality Evaluation Interface that supports both SDK and SBI scoring. * During biometric capture, if SDK is enabled and available, use the SDK-generated quality score. * Validate the SDK score against the existing configurable biometric quality threshold without modifying the current configuration flow. * If SDK is unavailable or disabled, automatically fall back to SBI quality score validation. * If SDK returns invalid responses, timeouts, or exceptions, block the registration flow and enforce biometric re-capture. * Add proper audit logging for SDK scores, SBI fallbacks, failures, and re-capture events. ### Mid-Point Deliverables * SDK integration framework * SDK score extraction and validation logic * Basic SBI fallback mechanism * Initial error handling and audit logging This approach keeps the implementation backward compatible while enabling real-time SDK-based biometric quality validation.

title: [C4GT Community]: Enhancement: Track Supervisor ID in Registration Packet Processing
content:
Problem description:
### Ticket Contents

## Description
As a registration system, I want to capture the supervisor ID along with approval/rejection actions during resident registration packet processing, so that country representatives can generate reports mapping supervisors to approved/rejected packets.

### Goals

## Goals
- [ ] Enable identification of the supervisor responsible for approving or rejecting registration packets.
- [ ] Ensure supervisor details are captured for audit and reporting purposes.
- [ ] Support accurate reporting of supervisor-wise approved and rejected packets.
- [ ] Strengthen validation by including supervisor verification during packet processing.

## You can refer to this link to know more about the registration client and the steps to follow for the installation:
- [Registration Client Overview](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-client)
- [Developers Guide](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-client/develop/registration-client-developers-guide)

### Expected Outcome

Supervisor ID is captured and stored whenever a packet is approved or rejected.
The system maintains a complete audit trail including supervisor comments and timestamps.
Country representatives can generate reports based on supervisor activity.
Packet processing enforces validation rules related to supervisor identification.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. **Supervisor Enablement & Access**
-   The user must be registered as a supervisor with valid credentials and supervisor ID.
-   The supervisor should be mapped to relevant centers and have access to view and process resident packets.

2. **Packet Approval/Rejection Flow**
The supervisor should be able to:
-   Log in to the registration client.
-   Navigate to the pending approval page.
-   View resident and packet details.
-   Approve or reject the packet with optional comments.

3. **Supervisor ID Capture**
When a supervisor approves a packet:

- The system must capture and store:
  Supervisor ID
  Approval status
  Supervisor comments (if any)
  Timestamp

- When a supervisor rejects a packet:
   The system must capture and store the same details as above.

4. **Admin Handling**
When an admin approves and uploads a packet:
- Admin ID must be captured and treated as the supervisor ID.
- Packets approved and uploaded by admins should be tracked and marked separately.

Validation rules should differ for:
- Supervisor-uploaded packets (validated)
- Admin-uploaded packets (validation skipped where applicable)

5. **Validation Mechanism**
- Supervisor validation must be included during packet processing.
- If supervisor ID is missing or null during approval/rejection:
       Packet validation must fail at the CMD stage.

6. **Reporting Capability**
The system administrator or country representative must be able to use supervisor ID to generate reports showing:

- Supervisor vs approved packets
- Supervisor vs rejected packets

title: [C4GT Community]: Define and Utilize Biometric Quality Through SDK or Default System
content:
Problem description:
### Ticket Contents

## Description
As a registration system, I want the registration client to define biometric quality using an SDK during biometric collection, so that the quality of captured biometrics is validated in real time and meets predefined standards.


### Goals

## Goals
- [ ] Enable integration of biometric quality evaluation through an SDK.
- [ ] Ensure real-time feedback on biometric quality during capture.
- [ ] Provide a fallback mechanism using SBI quality scores when SDK is unavailable.
- [ ] Maintain consistent validation and traceability of biometric quality checks.
You can refer to this link to know more about the registration client and the steps to follow for the installation:
[Registration Client Overview](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-client)
[Developers Guide](https://docs.mosip.io/1.2.0/id-lifecycle-management/identity-issuance/registration-client/develop/registration-client-developers-guide)


### Expected Outcome

Expected Outcome:

- Biometric quality is assessed in real time during capture.
- Operators are guided to re-capture biometrics if quality is insufficient.
- The system seamlessly falls back to SBI quality scores when SDK is unavailable.
- Registration is blocked if no valid quality score is available, ensuring data integrity.

### Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance Criteria:
1. SDK Integration for Quality Definition
-   The system should allow the registration client to integrate with an SDK for biometric quality evaluation.
-   The SDK must provide a real-time quality score during biometric capture.

title: Document Upload feature silently fails on modern Android 13+ tablets due to deprecated Storage Permissions
Login screen remains in navigation stack causing Back-Button Session Leak
content:
Problem description:
### Description
In `login_page.dart`, the navigation logic successfully routes the user to the `DashBoardTabletView` upon authentication. However, it utilizes `Navigator.of(context).push()` instead of a replacement method. 

Because `.push()` simply layers the new route on top of the existing one, the `LoginPage` remains active in the navigation stack. If an authenticated user presses the Android hardware Back button from the Dashboard, they are incorrectly routed back to the Login screen, breaking the session UX and creating an illogical app flow.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch the application and navigate to the Login screen.
2. Authenticate successfully to reach the Dashboard.
3. Press the physical hardware Back button on the Android device/emulator.
4. Observe that the app routes back to the Login screen instead of exiting the app or acting on the Dashboard's back-press logic.

### Expected Behavior
Once a user authenticates and navigates to the core application (Dashboard), the Login screen should be completely removed from the navigation stack. Pressing the Back button from the root Dashboard should either prompt the user to exit the app or do nothing, but it should never return to the Login screen.

### Environment
* **Target File:** `lib/ui/login_page.dart`

### Proposed Solution
Replace the `Navigator.of(context).push(...)` call with `Navigator.of(context).pushReplacement(...)` (or `pushAndRemoveUntil` if there are multiple pre-login routes) to ensure the authentication screens are destroyed upon successful login.

title: <Feature><Center Remap> US#05: Backend API Integration for Centre Remapping
content:
Problem description:
### Description

As a **Backend System**, I want to provide APIs that support centre remapping detection, packet upload, operator data upload, and mapping verification, So that Android client can seamlessly perform all centre remapping operations with data consistency.

### Purpose

To ensure Android client has reliable, secure backend support for all centre remapping operations.


### Pre-requisites

* Master sync API available
* Packet upload API available
* Operator management API available
* Authentication/authorization framework working
* API versioning strategy in place

### Basic Flow

**API 1: Master Sync with Remapping Indicator**
1. Android client calls: `GET /registration/v1/config/mastersync?machineId={id}&centreId={id}`
2. Backend identifies if machine mapped to different centre
3. Backend response includes:
   ```json
   {
     "centreRemapped": true,
     "oldCentreId": "...",
     "newCentreId": "...",
     "masterData": { ... },
     "timestamp": "..."
   }
   ```
4. Android client parses response; detects remapping indicator
5. All standard master data also included for sync

**API 2: Packet Upload (Existing, Enhanced for Remapping)**
1. Android client calls: `POST /registration/v1/packet/upload` with packets
2. Backend validates packets
3. Backend stores packets for processing
4. Backend responds with upload status for each packet
5. Works same as normal upload but during remapping flow

**API 3: Operator Data Upload**
1. Android client calls: `POST /registration/v1/operator/upload`
2. Backend receives operator credentials, biometrics, roles
3. Backend stores operator data (may deactivate old operator)
4. Backend confirms receipt and success

**API 4: Verify Centre Remapping Completion (Optional)**
1. Android client calls: `GET /registration/v1/centre/remap/status?machineId={id}`
2. Backend confirms remapping status
3. Response confirms old centre cleanup completed

### Alternate Flows

**Alternate Flow A1: API Response Timeout**
1. Android client calls API
2. Server takes >2 seconds to respond
3. Android client timeout triggers
4. Client retries request (exponential backoff)
5. Backend responds normally (no duplicate processing)

**Alternate Flow A2: Invalid/Corrupted API Response**
1. Android client receives response
2. Response missing required fields
3. Client logs error; treats as no remapping (conservative)
4. Sync continues normally; user not blocked

**Alternate Flow A3: Authentication Failure**
1. Android client calls API with invalid token
2. Backend returns 401 Unauthorized
3. Android client redirects to login
4. After login, retry API call

**Alternate Flow A4: Authorization Failure**
1. Android client calls operator upload API
2. Backend verifies user has permission
3. If denied: Returns 403 Forbidden
4. Android client shows error; allows contact support

### Scenarios

### Scenarios

| Scenario | Request | Response | Android Action |
|----------|---------|----------|---|
| S1 | Master sync; remapping detected | centreRemapped=true | Alert; set flag |
| S2 | Master sync; no remapping | centreRemapped=false | Normal flow |
| S3 | Packet upload; success | Success for each packet | Proceed to next |
| S4 | Packet upload; partial failure | Success/failure per packet | Retry failed packets |
| S5 | API timeout | 503 or timeout | Retry with backoff |
| S6 | Invalid response | Malformed JSON | Log error; treat conservatively |

---

### Error Messages

| Error Condition | HTTP Status | Message | Android Handling |
|---|---|---|---|
| Remapping check fails | 500 | Internal server error | Retry; treat as no remapping |
| Packet upload fails | 400 | Packet validation error | Show error; allow retry |
| Operator upload fails | 400 | Missing required field | Show error; allow retry |
| Authentication fails | 401 | Invalid token | Redirect to login |
| Authorization fails | 403 | Insufficient permissions | Show error; contact support |
| API timeout | 503 | Service unavailable | Retry with backoff |

### Data Fields

**Master Sync Response:**
```json
{
  "centreRemapped": boolean,
  "oldCentreId": "string",
  "newCentreId": "string",
  "masterData": {
    "templates": [],
    "devices": [],
    ...
  },
  "timestamp": "ISO-8601 datetime"
}
```

**Packet Upload Request:**
```json
{
  "packets": [
    {
      "packetId": "string",
      "fileName": "string",
      "fileSize": number,
      "checksumType": "string",
      "checksum": "string",
      "fileData": "base64"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Operator Data Upload Request:**
```json
{
  "operators": [
    {
      "operatorId": "string",
      "name": "string",
      "credentials": { ... },
      "biometrics": { ... },
      "roles": []
    }
  ]
}
```


### Business Rules (With Audit)

**BR-001:** All APIs MUST require authentication

**BR-002:** Master sync MUST always return centre mapping status (even if unchanged)

**BR-003:** Packet upload MUST support both single and batch uploads

**BR-004:** Operator upload MUST be atomic (all succeed or all fail)

**BR-005:** API responses MUST include timestamp for audit trail

**BR-006:** Invalid requests MUST return 400; not 500

**BR-007:** API MUST handle duplicate requests idempotently

### Acceptance Criteria

| Criteria | Verification |
|----------|---|
| Master sync includes remapping indicator | Call API; verify response structure |
| Packet upload works for remapping flow | Upload packets; verify stored correctly |
| Operator upload preserves all data | Upload; query database; verify fields |
| API handles errors gracefully | Simulate errors; verify appropriate responses |
| API handles timeouts | Delay response; verify client retries |
| Invalid responses handled conservatively | Send malformed response; verify client doesn't crash |

### Exceptions

_No response_

### Documentation

_No response_

### Reference UX

_No response_

### Compatibility

_No response_

### Implementation Details

**Endpoints to Create/Modify:**
* `GET /registration/v1/config/mastersync` - Add centreRemapped indicator
* `POST /registration/v1/packet/upload` - Already exists; ensure works during remapping
* `POST /registration/v1/operator/upload` - Create new endpoint
* `GET /registration/v1/centre/remap/status` - Create optional verification endpoint

**Validation Logic:**
* Verify request contains required fields
* Verify authentication token valid
* Verify user authorized for operation
* Validate packet data integrity (checksum)
* Validate operator data completeness

**Error Handling:**
* Map business logic errors to appropriate HTTP status codes
* Return detailed error messages for debugging
* Log all API calls for audit trail

---

### Definition of Done

- [ ] Master sync API returns remapping indicator
- [ ] Packet upload API tested with remapping flow
- [ ] Operator upload API created and tested
- [ ] All APIs authenticated and authorized
- [ ] API responses match defined contracts
- [ ] Error handling comprehensive
- [ ] Timeout handling implemented
- [ ] Idempotency verified
- [ ] API documentation updated
- [ ] Unit tests for each endpoint (>80% coverage)
- [ ] Integration tests with Android client
- [ ] Load testing performed
- [ ] Security review completed
- [ ] Code reviewed
- [ ] Deployed to staging environment
- [ ] Tested with actual Android client
- [ ] Documented for Android team

### Non-Functional Requirements

| Requirement | Specification |
|------------|---|
| Response Time | <2 seconds for all APIs |
| Availability | 99.9% uptime |
| Scalability | Handle 1000 concurrent requests |
| Security | Encrypted communication; no credential exposure |
| Audit Trail | All operations logged |

title: <Feature><Centre Remap> US#04:Execute Centre Remapping Cleanup
content:
Problem description:
### Description

As a **System**, I want to orchestrate a multi-step cleanup process that uploads pending data, deletes centre-specific records, and resets the remapping state, So that the device is fully transitioned to the new centre without data loss or inconsistency.

### Purpose

To ensure complete, consistent, and irreversible transition from old centre to new centre with all data preserved on server before local deletion.


### Pre-requisites

* Centre remapping flag is set ([issue-1045](https://github.com/mosip/android-registration-client/issues/1045))
* No pending approval packets remain
* Device is online
* All previous cleanup steps successful (if resuming)

### Basic Flow

**Step 1: Verify Preconditions**
1. System checks if device is online (throws error if offline)
2. System checks if any active registration operations in progress (blocks if true)
3. System checks GLOBAL_PARAM for remapping flag (must be true)
4. System acquires cleanup lock to prevent concurrent cleanups
5. If all checks pass, proceeds to Step 2

**Step 2: Upload Pending Packets**
1. System queries all registration packets with status PROCESSING or RE-SEND
2. System displays progress dialog: "Uploading packets. Please don't close the application"
3. System uploads each packet to server
4. On success: Marks packet as uploaded; proceeds to next packet
5. On failure: Retries up to 5 times with exponential backoff (1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, 16s)
6. If all retries fail: Throws UploadFailedException; stops sync; allows retry
7. When all packets uploaded: Updates AUDIT with success; proceeds to Step 3

**Step 3: Upload Operator Onboarding Data**
1. System queries all operator records for current centre
2. System uploads operator data (credentials, biometrics, roles) to server
3. Retry logic same as Step 2
4. On success: Proceeds to Step 4
5. On failure: Throws exception; allows retry

**Step 4: Delete Pre-registration Data**
1. System queries all PRE_REGISTRATION records
2. System deletes all pre-registration packet files from disk
3. System deletes all PRE_REGISTRATION database records (within transaction)
4. System deletes associated metadata
5. Logs count of deleted records in AUDIT
6. Proceeds to Step 5

**Step 5: Delete Registration Packets (Specific Statuses Only)**
1. System queries registration packets with status: PROCESSING, PROCESSED, RE-REGISTER
2. Note: DOES NOT delete packets with status RECEIVED or RE-SEND
3. System deletes matching packet files
4. System deletes matching database records (within transaction)
5. Logs detailed deletion counts in AUDIT
6. Proceeds to Step 6

**Step 6: Delete Centre-Specific Master Data**
1. System deletes centre-specific document types
2. System deletes centre-specific device registrations
3. System deletes centre-specific templates/configurations
4. Note: DOES NOT delete GLOBAL_PARAM (global) or AUDIT (immutable)
5. Uses transaction to ensure atomicity
6. Logs deletion summary in AUDIT
7. Proceeds to Step 7

**Step 7: Remove All Operators for Current Centre**
1. System queries all OPERATOR records for current centre
2. System deletes OPERATOR records
3. System deletes OPERATOR_BIOMETRIC records
4. System deletes OPERATOR_ROLE records
5. System deletes operator preferences
6. If current operator is logged in: Forces logout
7. Logs operator IDs deleted in AUDIT
8. Proceeds to Step 8

**Step 8: Reset Remapping Flag and Re-enable Auto-sync**
1. System updates GLOBAL_PARAM: sets `mosip.registration.centermappedchanged` to 'false'
2. System clears SessionContext.centreRemapped flag
3. System re-enables automatic sync scheduling
4. System releases cleanup lock
5. Logs completion with full statistics in AUDIT
6. Displays success message on screen

### Alternate Flows

**Alternate Flow A1: Offline During Sync**
1. Sync is running (e.g., at Step 3 uploading operator data)
2. Device loses connectivity
3. System detects offline condition
4. Current step is rolled back (transaction)
5. System pauses cleanup and saves state (last completed step = 2)
6. System displays dialog: "System went offline. Sync paused. Will resume when online."
7. When connectivity restored:
   * System displays: "Connectivity restored. Resuming cleanup..."
   * System resumes from Step 3 (continues from next step after last completed)
   * Remaining steps execute normally
8. Cleanup completes successfully

**Alternate Flow A2: Cleanup Failure at Any Step**
1. Step fails (e.g., database deletion throws error)
2. System catches exception
3. System rolls back transaction (no partial deletion)
4. System saves failure state in CLEANUP_STATE table
5. System displays error dialog with user-friendly message
6. Dialog includes:
   * What failed (e.g., "Failed to delete pre-registration data")
   * Why it failed (e.g., "Disk space low")
   * "RETRY" button to restart from failed step
   * "CONTACT SUPPORT" button to show error details
7. User clicks RETRY:
   * System resumes from failed step
   * If successful: Continues normally
   * If fails again: Shows error again with retry option

**Alternate Flow A3: App Crashes During Cleanup**
1. Cleanup is running (e.g., at Step 4)
2. App crashes or is terminated
3. Cleanup state is saved to CLEANUP_STATE table (before each step)
4. On app restart:
   * System detects incomplete cleanup (flag still true)
   * System shows dialog: "Previous cleanup interrupted. Resume?"
   * Options: "RESUME" (continues from last completed step) or "START OVER"
   * If user selects RESUME:
     - Loads cleanup state from database
     - Continues from Step 5 (last completed was Step 4)
     - Completes normally

**Alternate Flow A4: Multiple Cleanup Attempts**
1. First cleanup attempt partially succeeds (completes Steps 1-4, fails on Step 5)
2. User retries cleanup
3. System resumes from Step 5
4. Completes remaining steps
5. Success

**Alternate Flow A5: Cleanup Completes Successfully**
1. All 8 steps complete
2. System displays success dialog with statistics:
   - Pre-registration packets deleted: 23
   - Registration packets deleted: 156
   - Operators removed: 5
   - Cleanup completed at: 2:45 PM
3. Dialog has "CLOSE" button
4. User clicks CLOSE
5. System navigates to home screen
6. All blocked operations now available
7. Centre Remapping menu option disappears

### Scenarios

### Scenarios

| Scenario | Flow | Expected Result |
|----------|------|---|
| S1 | Normal cleanup: online, no interruptions | All steps complete; success message |
| S2 | Offline at Step 3 | Pause and resume when online; complete |
| S3 | Failure at Step 5 (database error) | Error shown; retry available |
| S4 | App crash at Step 4 | State saved; resume option on restart |
| S5 | User retries from failed attempt | Resume from failure point; complete |
| S6 | Network timeout during upload (Step 2) | Auto-retry with backoff; eventually succeed |

---

### Error Messages

| Step | Error Condition | Message | Recovery |
|------|---|---|---|
| Step 1-2 | Upload fails after retries | "Failed to upload packets. Please check your connection and retry." | Retry button |
| Step 4 | Disk space insufficient | "Insufficient storage for sync. Please free up space." | Manual cleanup of files; retry |
| Step 6 | Database locked | "System busy. Please wait and retry." | Automatic retry |
| General | Network offline during cleanup | "Device went offline. Sync will resume when online." | Auto-resume |
| General | Permission denied | "System permission required for sync. Please contact administrator." | Contact support |

### Data Fields

| Field | Purpose | Updated At |
|-------|---------|---|
| Last completed step | Tracks progress for resume | After each step |
| Error details | Logging and recovery | When error occurs |
| Deleted packet count | Audit statistics | After deletion step |
| Deleted operator count | Audit statistics | After operator deletion |
| Cleanup start timestamp | Audit trail | Step 1 |
| Cleanup end timestamp | Audit trail | Step 8 |

### Business Rules (With Audit)

**BR-001:** Cleanup MUST execute steps in exact order; no skipping or reordering

**BR-002:** Before cleanup starts:
* Device MUST be online
* No active registration operations
* Remapping flag MUST be true
* No pending approval packets

**BR-003:** Each deletion MUST be atomic (transaction); no partial deletions

**BR-004:** Upload MUST complete before any deletion begins (data safety first)

**BR-005:** Operators cannot login after deletion (Step 7)

**BR-006:** GLOBAL_PARAM and AUDIT tables MUST NEVER be deleted

**BR-007:** Cleanup state MUST be persisted after each step (for resume capability)

**BR-008:** All cleanup steps MUST be logged in AUDIT table

**BR-009:** On success, remapping flag MUST be reset (Step 8)

**BR-010:** Auto-sync MUST be re-enabled after success (Step 8)

### Acceptance Criteria

| Criteria | Verification |
|----------|---|
| All steps execute in correct order | Audit logs show sequence |
| No data loss; all uploaded packets before deletion | Verify server has data; local deleted |
| Offline detected and cleanup paused | Disconnect network; observe pause |
| Cleanup resumed correctly after offline | Restore connection; verify continuation |
| Failure at any step shows error; allows retry | Simulate failure; verify error dialog |
| App crash saves state; resume option works | Force crash; restart app; verify resume |
| Success message shows accurate statistics | Calculate expected counts; verify displayed |
| GLOBAL_PARAM and AUDIT untouched | Query database post-cleanup |
| Operators cannot login post-cleanup | Attempt login with old credentials; verify blocked |
| Auto-sync re-enabled after success | Verify sync scheduler running |

### Exceptions

| Exception | Handling | Recovery |
|-----------|----------|----------|
| Offline detected | Roll back current transaction; pause | Resume when online |
| Upload failure | Retry up to 5x with backoff | Allow manual retry if all fail |
| Database error | Roll back transaction; log error | Manual retry after fixing issue |
| Permission denied | Log error; show message | Contact support; manual intervention |
| App crash | Save state to database | Auto-resume on restart |

### Documentation

_No response_

### Reference UX

_No response_

### Compatibility

_No response_

### Implementation Details

**Files to Create:**
* `lib/services/registration/centre_remapping_service.dart` (main orchestration)
* `lib/models/remapping_result.dart`
* `lib/models/remapping_stats.dart`
* `lib/models/cleanup_progress.dart`
* `lib/models/cleanup_state.dart`

**Files to Modify:**
* `lib/repositories/registration_packet_repository.dart` - Add queries and delete methods
* `lib/repositories/pre_registration_repository.dart` - Add delete methods
* `lib/repositories/operator_repository.dart` - Add delete methods
* `lib/repositories/cleanup_state_repository.dart` - Create for state persistence
* `lib/services/sync_service.dart` - Use for packet upload
* `lib/utils/audit_logger.dart` - Add cleanup event types
* `lib/utils/session_context.dart` - Track cleanup progress
* `lib/db/database_helper.dart` - Transaction management

**Key Implementation Points:**
* Use database transactions for atomicity
* Implement step-by-step state saving for resume capability
* Network connectivity monitoring for pause/resume
* Comprehensive audit logging at each step
* User-friendly error messages with recovery options

---

### Definition of Done

- [ ] Centre remapping service created with all 8 steps
- [ ] Step orchestration logic correct
- [ ] Transaction management for atomicity working
- [ ] Offline detection and pause/resume logic implemented
- [ ] Cleanup state persistence working (resume capability)
- [ ] Upload retry logic with exponential backoff
- [ ] Audit logging for all steps complete
- [ ] Error handling for each step
- [ ] Success/failure messages clear and actionable
- [ ] Unit tests for each step (>80% coverage)
- [ ] Integration test for full cleanup flow
- [ ] Integration test for offline scenarios
- [ ] Integration test for failure recovery
- [ ] Integration test for app crash recovery
- [ ] Manual testing with actual packet data
- [ ] Performance testing (verify <15 min duration)
- [ ] Data integrity verification (query database post-cleanup)
- [ ] Code reviewed by 2+ senior developers
- [ ] Code merged with no warnings

### Non-Functional Requirements

| Requirement | Specification |
|------------|---|
| Sync Duration | <15 minutes for 500 packets |
| Data Consistency | 100% accuracy; no corruption |
| Reliability | No data loss even on crash |
| Auditability | Complete trail of all operations |
| Error Recovery | Auto-resume capability |
| Security | Only authenticated cleanup; no bypass |

title: <Feature><Center Remap Sync> US#03: Display Centre Remapping Status
content:
Problem description:
### Description

As an **Operator**, I want to see a clear status screen showing the progress of the sync process, So that I understand what actions I can and cannot take .

### Purpose

To provide operators with clear visibility into the remapping state and guide them through the required process.

### Pre-requisites

- Centre remapping flag must be set (from [issue-1045](https://github.com/mosip/android-registration-client/issues/1045))
- Centre remapping menu option visible (from [issue-1046](https://github.com/mosip/android-registration-client/issues/1046))
- Status screen accessible from menu
- Database queries for packet counts working
- Network connectivity status available

### Basic Flow

1. Operator clicks "Centre Remapping" menu option
2. System displays Centre Remapping Status Screen showing:

   **Section 1: Status Header**
   - Title: "Centre Remapping in Progress"
   - Status indicator: Current centre mapping state
   - Timestamp: When remapping was detected

   **Section 2: Pending Activities Count**
   - Packets awaiting upload: X
   - Packets pending operator approval: Y
   - Packets in processing state: Z

   **Section 3: Blocked Operations**
   - [Blocked] New Registration
   - [Blocked] UIN Update
   - [Blocked] Lost UIN
   - [Blocked] Operator Onboarding
   - [Blocked] Biometric Update
   - [Blocked] Pre-registration Download

   **Section 4: Allowed Operations**
   - [Allowed] Approve Pending Packets
   - [Allowed] Manual Sync
   - [Allowed] Export Packets

   **Section 5: System Status**
   - Connectivity: Online/Offline indicator
   - Last sync timestamp

   **Section 6: Action Button**
   - "Sync Centre" button enabled ONLY if:
     * System is ONLINE
     * No pending approval packets remain (Y = 0)
   - If disabled, tooltip explains: "Please complete pending approvals and ensure online connectivity before starting cleanup"

3. Operator reviews the status
4. Operator completes pending approvals (via Packet Approval screen)

title: Unhandled FormatException crash during JSON decoding in NetworkService
content:
Problem description:
### Description
In `NetworkServiceImpl.getVersionNoApp()`, the application parses the network response directly using `jsonDecode(response.body)` without a surrounding `try-catch` block for format exceptions.

While the code checks for `response.statusCode == 200`, this does not guarantee the payload is valid JSON. If a proxy, firewall, or server misconfiguration intercepts the request and returns an HTML payload or an empty string with a 200 status, `jsonDecode` will immediately throw a fatal `FormatException` (e.g., `Unexpected character`). Because this exception is unhandled, it bypasses the normal error flow and causes a hard application crash.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Intercept the network request to the actuator endpoint (using a tool like Charles Proxy or Postman).
2. Return a `200 OK` status, but change the response body to an empty string `""` or a basic HTML string `<html>Error</html>`.
3. Trigger the network call in the app.
4. Observe the immediate `FormatException` and fatal runtime crash in the console.

### Expected Behavior
Network payloads must be treated as untrusted data. `jsonDecode` should be wrapped in a `try-catch` block specifically catching `FormatException`. If parsing fails, the app should gracefully handle it (e.g., returning a default value or showing an error UI) instead of crashing.

### Environment
* **Target File:** `network_service_impl.dart`

### Proposed Solution
Wrap the `jsonDecode` logic inside a `try-catch` block. Catch the `FormatException`, log the parsing error, and handle the failure state safely without bringing down the application.

title: UnsupportedError crash due to fixed-length List.empty() initialization in Service implementations
content:
Problem description:
### Description
Across several service implementations (e.g., `BiometricsServiceImpl`, `ProcessSpecServiceImpl`), lists are initialized using `List.empty()` inside `try-catch` blocks as fallback values when an API call fails. 

In Dart, `List.empty()` defaults to `growable: false`. This creates a strictly fixed-length list of size 0. If the UI layer or state management providers later attempt to append items to these lists using `.add()` or `.addAll()`, the application will immediately crash with an `UnsupportedError (Cannot add to a fixed-length list)`.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a method that returns `List.empty()` on failure (e.g., `getBiometrics` or `getNewProcessSpec`).
2. Simulate a network or platform exception so the `catch` block executes.
3. Have the consuming UI provider attempt to append a new item to the returned list (`list.add(newItem)`).
4. Observe the runtime crash and `UnsupportedError` in the console.

### Expected Behavior
Fallback empty lists should be growable so that consuming UI layers can safely interact with them without causing runtime exceptions.

### Environment
* **Target Files:** `biometrics_service_impl.dart`, `process_spec_service_impl.dart`, `document_category_impl.dart`, etc.

### Proposed Solution
Replace all instances of `List.empty()` with the standard growable list literal `[]` (or explicitly use `List.empty(growable: true)`).

title: Application crash due to LateInitializationError in service implementations
content:
Problem description:
### Description
Multiple service implementation files (e.g., `AuthServiceImpl`, `MachineKeyImpl`, `SyncResponseServiceImpl`) use the `late` keyword for variables that are assigned within `try-catch` blocks. When a `PlatformException` or any other error occurs during a native API call, the variable remains uninitialized. However, the methods still attempt to return these variables, leading to an immediate `LateInitializationError` and an application crash.

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Trigger a service method that uses a `late` variable (e.g., `AuthServiceImpl.validateUser` or `MachineKeyImpl.getMachineKeys`).
2. Simulate a failure in the underlying Pigeon API call (e.g., disconnect the device or mock a `PlatformException`).
3. The `catch` block will log the error, but the method will proceed to return the uninitialized variable.
4. Observe the app crash with `LateInitializationError: Field '...' has not been initialized`.

### Expected Behavior
Service methods should handle API failures gracefully. They should either:
* Return a nullable type (e.g., `Future<User?>`) so the UI can handle the absence of data.
* Return a default/empty instance of the object instead of leaving a `late` variable uninitialized.

### Environment
* **Target Files:** `auth_service_impl.dart`, `machine_key_service_impl.dart`, `sync_response_service_impl.dart`, `registration_service_impl.dart`, etc.

### Proposed Solution
1. Modify the abstract interfaces in the `platform_spi` layer to allow nullable return types where appropriate.
2. In the implementation files, remove the `late` keyword.
3. Initialize variables with default values or change them to nullable types and return `null` in the `catch` block.

title: <Feature><Center Rempa Sync> US#02: Block Registration Operations When Centre Remapping is In Progress
content:
Problem description:
### Description

As a System, I want to prevent operators from performing registration-related operations once their machine has been remapped to another centre by the Admin, So that no new data is created or modified under an incorrect centre context until the remap sync is completed.

### Purpose

To ensure data integrity by restricting all critical operations immediately after centre remapping and until the operator completes the Centre Remap Sync process.

### Pre-requisites

- Centre remapping must be detected and flagged in the system
- SessionContext must contain a property indicating remap status
- Dashboard and navigation flows must be implemented
- State management mechanism must be available to propagate remap status

### Basic Flow

**For New Registration:**
- Operator logs into the application
- System detects that the machine has been remapped to another centre
- System sets the remap flag in SessionContext
- Operator attempts to tap the “New Registration” button on the home screen
- System checks the remap flag
- Since the operator is remapped:
- when he clicks on new registration then an error message to be displayed : “New registration is not allowed as the machine has been remapped. Please complete the Centre Remap Sync.”
- No navigation to the registration screen is allowed
- System logs the blocked attempt in audit logs

The same behavior applies to the following operations:
- UIN Update
- Lost UIN
- Operator Onboarding
- Biometric Update
- Pre-registration Download

### Alternate Flows

**Alternate Flow 1- When remapping is detected during an active session:**
If the operator is already logged in and the system detects remapping during a background sync or metadata refresh, the system updates the remap flag immediately. All relevant buttons on the dashboard are dynamically disabled. If the operator is currently inside any restricted screen, the system shows a blocking dialog explaining that operations are no longer allowed and navigates the user back to the home screen.

**Alternate Flow 2- When the operator attempts multiple restricted operations:**
If the operator tries multiple restricted actions one after another, each attempt is blocked independently. The system displays the relevant message for each operation and logs each attempt separately for audit purposes.

**Alternate Flow 3- When remap sync is completed successfully:**
After the operator completes the Centre Remap Sync process, the system resets the remap flag. All previously restricted operations become available again. The UI updates automatically, enabling all buttons and restoring normal functionality.

### Scenarios

| Scenario | Action | Expected Result |
|----------|--------|-----------------|
| S1 | Operator clicks New Registration while remapped | blocking message displayed |
| S2 | Operator clicks UIN Update while remapped | Blocking message displayed |
| S3 | Operator clicks Lost UIN while remapped | Blocking message displayed |
| S4 | Operator clicks Operator Onboarding while remapped | Blocking message shown |
| S5 | Operator clicks Biometric Update while remapped | Biometric capture prevented; blocking message shown |
| S6 | Operator attempts Pre-registration Download while remapped | Download blocked; message explains why |
| S7 | Cleanup completes and flag reset; operator retries operation | Operation proceeds normally |
| S8 | Operator navigates back/uses deep link to forced access screen | Route guard blocks; dialog forces return to home |


### Error Messages

| Operation | Message |
|-----------|---------|
| New Registration | "New registration is not allowed while centre remapping is in progress." |
| UIN Update | "UIN update is not allowed while centre remapping is in progress." |
| Lost UIN | "Lost UIN report is not allowed while centre remapping is in progress." |
| Operator Onboarding | "Operator onboarding is not allowed while centre remapping is in progress." |
| Biometric Update | "Biometric update is not allowed while centre remapping is in progress." |
| Pre-registration Download | "Pre-registration download is not available during centre remapping." |

### Data Fields

_No response_

### Business Rules (With Audit)

- All registration-related operations must be blocked immediately once remapping is detected
- Blocking must be enforced at multiple levels:
  - User Interface level by disabling buttons
  - Navigation level by restricting screen access
  - Service level by validating before execution
- All blocked attempts must be logged with operator details and timestamp
- The restriction remains active until Centre Remap Sync is successfully completed
- The system must clearly communicate the reason for restriction to the operator
