title: RCF-1239: Enable document upload in Android Registration Client through the Inji application
content:
Problem description:
*Title:* Enable document upload in Android Registration Client through the Inji application

*User Story:*

*As a* Registration Operator / Supervisor

*I want to* upload and submit required supporting documents (such as proof of identity, address, or birth certificate) through the *Inji application*, which are then seamlessly linked to the corresponding registration record in the *Android Registration Client*

*So that I can c*omplete my registration process digitally without needing to physically present or manually transfer documents, ensuring a faster, more secure, and paperless registration experience.

*Background / Context:*

The *Android Registration Client (ARC)* is used for resident registration and biometric capture in offline or semi-connected environments. Currently, operators or residents must manually add or scan documents using the client device’s camera or external sources. To enhance user experience and efficiency, this feature enables *document upload directly via Inji*, the resident-facing app, which communicates securely with the Android Registration Client to transfer and associate uploaded documents with the ongoing registration session.

This capability supports digital-first enrolment, remote document submission, and improved verification processes, especially in assisted or self-registration scenarios.

*Basic Flow:*

1. *Initiation from Inji:*
#* The resident logs into *Inji* and navigates to the document upload section linked to their UIN.
#* The resident selects one or more document categories (e.g., Proof of Identity, Proof of Address, Proof of Birth).

1. *Document Upload:*
#* The resident can upload documents by:
#** Taking a photo using the phone camera
#** Selecting an existing file from the gallery or file manager
#* Inji validates the file format and size before upload (e.g., JPEG, PNG, PDF; up to 5 MB per file).

1. *Secure Transfer to ARC:*
#* Uploaded documents are encrypted and securely transferred to the Android Registration Client via an established communication channel (e.g., local network, QR-based session link, or secure relay).
#* The ARC associates the received documents with the relevant registration packet (based on registration ID or session token).

1. *Operator Verification:*
#* The registration operator can view the uploaded documents within the ARC interface.
#* Operators can verify the completeness and clarity of documents before proceeding with biometric capture or demographic validation.

1. *Acknowledgment:*
#* Once documents are successfully linked, the resident receives an acknowledgment in Inji confirming the upload status.
#* In case of errors (e.g., network failure, format issue), Inji displays a clear error message and allows retry.

*Acceptance Criteria:*

1. *Document Types and Format Support*
#* The system shall allow upload of JPEG, PNG, and PDF files.
#* The maximum size per document shall not exceed 5 MB.
#* Each registration session must allow upload of multiple document categories.

1. *Security*
#* All documents shall be encrypted in transit and at rest.
#* The linkage between Inji and ARC shall use a secure token or QR-based session identifier.
#* ARC shall only accept documents from authenticated Inji sessions.

1. *Usability*
#* The user should receive clear progress indicators during upload and confirmation messages upon success.
#* If upload fails, the user should see actionable error messages (e.g., “Upload failed due to network issue. Please retry.”)

1. *Integration*
#* The ARC must automatically attach received documents to the correct registration record.
#* Uploaded documents should appear in the operator’s view under the appropriate document category.

1. *Offline Handling*
#* If ARC is offline, the uploaded documents should be queued in Inji for sync when connection is restored.

1. *Audit & Logs*
#* Both Inji and ARC shall maintain logs of upload events (timestamp, document type, registration ID, status).

*Non-Functional Requirements:*

- *Performance:* Upload should complete within 10 seconds on a 4G connection for a 2 MB file.

- *Scalability:* System should support concurrent uploads from multiple Inji clients.

- *Accessibility:* UI should comply with accessibility guidelines (clear labels, high contrast, multilingual support).

*Dependencies:*

- Active Inji-ARC communication interface (API or local pairing mechanism)

- Updated ARC version supporting document ingestion endpoint

- Inji app release with document upload and session linking capability

*Example Scenario:*

1. Resident initiates registration at a local center.

1. Operator creates a registration session and displays a QR code on ARC.

1. Resident scans the QR code using Inji to link the session.

1. Resident uploads ID proof and address proof documents from their phone.

1. Documents appear in the ARC under the “Documents” section, attached to the resident’s record.

1. Operator verifies and continues registration.

1. Resident receives confirmation in Inji: “Documents successfully uploaded and linked to your registration.”

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: **Jira Assignee:** Pragya (no valid GitHub user found)

title: RCF-1399: Security testing: ARC - data protection in case of loss of device
content:
Problem description:
## 🔗 Linked Issues

### ISSUE
- **MOSIP-34357**
  Status: New

Discussion and resolution:
[Ivanmeneges]: Anusha sunkada commented: # App data:
## Shared preferences - what is stored in plain shared preferences? [~accountid:624d6feef3824d006a5c6519] 
## Sqlite DB - DB is encrypted with randomly generated password, password in rest is in encryptedSharedPreferences.
# Registration packets - It is already encrypted envelopes, hence no harm, Also on disaster recovery, we will need this to be accessible so that packets can be uploaded in the admin portal.
# PreRegistration packets - is it encrypted packet stored as is in the external storage?  [~accountid:624d6feef3824d006a5c6519] 
# Acknowledgment slips (html/pdf?) - is it stored in DB or external storage?  [~accountid:624d6feef3824d006a5c6519] 



[~accountid:712020:1caf7501-caf0-450e-b281-e1ceded02e38]  - should we consider any other data other than 4 listed above?

cc: [~accountid:5fc884940d2f61006fb351f4]

[Ivanmeneges]: Madhu commented: # In plain shared preferences, only the logged language key is stored.
# Pre-registration packets - Re‑encrypted locally with AES‑GCM and saved under the app’s internal files directory, not SD‑card/shared external storage.
# Acknowledgement slips (HTML/pdf?) - acknowledgement slips are HTML, which is stored temporarily in encrypted secure storage, not in the DB and not on external storage.
# PDF is created on demand when the user taps Print, using the {{printing}} package ({{Printing.layoutPdf}} / {{Printing.convertHtml}}) from the same HTML.

CC: [~accountid:557058:c955df2b-1615-45f5-8565-cbf63d54c49e]

[Ivanmeneges]: Madhu commented: [~accountid:712020:1caf7501-caf0-450e-b281-e1ceded02e38] , please check and provide your inputs.

[Ivanmeneges]: Mahesh Binayak commented: [~accountid:624d6feef3824d006a5c6519]  [~accountid:557058:c955df2b-1615-45f5-8565-cbf63d54c49e] 
a few extending questions .
1 . What is this language key we are storing in shared preferences ? is it just the name of a lang? why are we storing it at all ?
2. Pre-reg packets , how are you using aes-gcm ? what is the size of these packets usually ?
 a.  Are you using StrongBox or TEE-backed security to ensure keys are physically isolated in a dedicated hardware chip?

 b. Are you using a unique 12-byte IV for every single encryption operation to prevent pattern-matching attacks? 

 c. Are you concerned about data swapping between accounts , i.e internal exchange of keys at all ? 
3. Ack slips (HTML) are not encrypted themselves ? Stored in ESS ? only visible to logged in user ? shareable / non-shareable ?
4. When the apk is active and device is unlocked, what portion of sensitive data is on the RAM  unencrypted and for how long ?

5. No Mention of registration packets in the response [~accountid:624d6feef3824d006a5c6519] , how do we recover them in case of disaster ? do we also do any extra encryption there ?

[Ivanmeneges]: Madhu commented: # The key name language_code is a locale string (such as "en" or "ar") that represents the user’s selected UI language. It is stored to preserve the chosen app language even after the app restarts*.*
# Pre-reg packets & AES-GCM:
## Server pre-reg data is decrypted (e.g. via ClientCryptoManagerService), then re-encrypted on-device with AES-256-GCM (AES/GCM/NoPadding, 128-bit GCM tag, 12-byte random IV per encryption, no AAD). A 256-bit AES key is generated per packet and stored separately (e.g. URL-safe base64 in PreRegistrationDto). Implementation: CryptoManagerServiceImpl.symmetricEncryptWithRandomIV() / symmetricDecrypt(); pre-reg flow in PreRegZipHandlingServiceImpl.encryptAndSavePreRegPacket() and decryptPreRegPacket().
# Pre-reg packet size
## Max zip size: 200 KB. Max entries: 15. Compression ratio limit: 10 (zip-bomb mitigation). Enforced in PreRegZipHandlingServiceImpl; no “typical” size in code, only these limits.
# Ack slips are plain HTML, not encrypted by the app; a copy is stored in encrypted secure storage (ESS). They are only shown after login, with FLAG_SECURE, and the app does not provide sharing—only print.
# Sensitive data in RAM when the APK is active, and the device is unlocked:
When the app is running and the device is unlocked, all of the following sensitive data is held in RAM in unencrypted form:
## Demographics, documents, and biometrics for the current registration (in native {{RegistrationDto}}): kept until process kill or the next successful packet submit; not cleared on logout.
## Auth token (native SessionManager/prefs): kept until logout, then removed from prefs.
## Ack slip HTML, pre-reg data, and preview template (Flutter providers): cleared only on auto-logout or process kill; manual logout does not clear this Flutter state.
## Login password (Flutter login screen): kept from input until the user leaves the login screen; not explicitly cleared after successful login.
## Pre-reg decrypted packet and symmetric key: in memory only while the pre-reg flow is active.
Data is cleared only when: 
The app explicitly clears it (e.g., token on logout; Flutter registration state on auto-logout only; native registration DTO on successful submit or when starting a new registration), or the process is killed. Manual logout does not clear the in-memory registration data (demographics/documents/biometrics) on the native side, nor the Flutter registration/ack/pre-reg state; those can remain in RAM until process death or the next submit/start registration.
# Registration packets are mentioned by Anusha here - [https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/RCF-1399?focusedCommentId=133830|https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/RCF-1399?focusedCommentId=133830|smart-link] 


CC: [~accountid:5fc884940d2f61006fb351f4] [~accountid:557058:c955df2b-1615-45f5-8565-cbf63d54c49e]

[Ivanmeneges]: Mahesh Binayak commented: [~accountid:624d6feef3824d006a5c6519]  / [~accountid:557058:c955df2b-1615-45f5-8565-cbf63d54c49e] 
the app seems to be in over-retention mode. i.e it is storing data even after manual logouts and auto log outs, for our PII data to be safe , we should be triggering manual data wipes or cleanup commands to clean up the same. 
Some Technical change , we will need here. right ?
Pls share your thoughts .

Also [~accountid:624d6feef3824d006a5c6519] for pre-reg packets to be decrypted, where are u storing the prereg base key, and how often are we syncing that ?
also can it have multiple keys, as in the background multiple keys may have been used to create successive pre-reg packets?
where do u store those and how ?

[Ivanmeneges]: Madhu commented: [~accountid:5fc884940d2f61006fb351f4] Pre-reg packets are stored in the local secured DB, where all other (like master data, audit logs) are stored. The sync will happen depending on the corn jobs, and we can also do the manual sync.

[Ivanmeneges]: Mahesh Binayak commented: [~accountid:624d6feef3824d006a5c6519] does manual sync update the keys ?
I understand the pre-reg packets are stored in DB, however  when does the decryption happen ? after syncing these, right >
so where do we store the keys ? how many keys do we store ? etc

title: RCF-1402: Inactive Locations Displayed in Android Registration Client
content:
Problem description:
The masterdata.location table uses the boolean field *is_active* to control whether a location should be visible in the UI.

- When is_active = true → location should be shown

- When is_active = false → location should NOT be shown

This behavior works correctly in the Desktop Registration Client.

However, in the Android Registration Client, locations marked as inactive (is_active = false) are still rendered in the dropdown.

### Test Scenario

When selecting:
State: *Arcturus*

A simplified master.location table below:

| Code | name | hierarchy_level | hierarchy_level_name | parent_loc_code | lang_code | is_active |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ML | MotherLand | 0 | country |  | eng | true |
| AS | Arcturus | 1 | state | ML | eng | true |
| PS | Poinsettia | 2 | city | AS | eng | false |
| SM | Stramonium | 2 | city | AS | eng | true |

### Observed Behavior

*Android Registration Client:*

Both cities are displayed in the dropdown:

- Poinsettia (should NOT be shown)

- Stramonium 

*Desktop Registration Client:*

Only active city is displayed:

- Stramonium 

### Expected Behavior

The Android Registration Client should display *only locations where is_active = true*, consistent with Desktop Registration Client behavior.

For State: Arcturus → City dropdown should contain:

- Stramonium only

title: [DMP 2026]: Telemetry for Android Registration Client
content:
Problem description:
### Ticket Contents

## Description
This feature focuses on implementing a telemetry system within the Flutter-based Android Registration Client to collect data on user behavior and application performance.

Currently, there is limited visibility into how users interact with the application and where performance issues may occur. By integrating telemetry, the system will enable data-driven decision-making, helping product and engineering teams identify usage patterns, detect bottlenecks, monitor crashes, and continuously improve the user experience.

The feature will ensure that telemetry data is collected securely, respects user privacy, and can be configured based on deployment needs.


### Goals & Mid-Point Milestone

## Goals

### **Overall Goals**

* Integrate a telemetry library/service into the Flutter application
* Capture user interaction events (clicks, navigation, flows)
* Collect application performance metrics (startup time, response latency)
* Capture device metadata (model, OS version, app version)
* Log errors, exceptions, and crash reports
* Enable secure transmission of telemetry data to backend systems
* Ensure compliance with privacy regulations (user consent, opt-in/opt-out)
* Provide dashboards and reporting for analysis
* Ensure minimal performance overhead due to telemetry

### **Mid-Point Milestone**

* Basic telemetry SDK integration in Flutter app
* Capture core user events (screen navigation, key actions)
* Capture basic performance metrics (app startup time)
* Implement error and crash logging
* Backend endpoint integration for telemetry ingestion
* Basic configuration toggle to enable/disable telemetry


### Setup/Installation

_No response_

### Expected Outcome

The final implementation will provide a **robust and scalable telemetry framework** embedded within the Flutter application:

* The system will automatically capture and log **user interactions**, enabling visibility into user journeys and feature usage
* **Performance metrics** such as app startup time, API response times, and screen load times will be tracked continuously
* **Crash reports and error logs** will be collected to help quickly identify and debug issues
* Telemetry data will be **securely transmitted and stored** in backend systems for further analysis
* Users will have control over telemetry collection through **consent mechanisms and configuration settings**
* Product and engineering teams will be able to access **dashboards and reports** to analyze trends, detect anomalies, and make informed decisions
* The telemetry system will be optimized to ensure **no noticeable degradation in app performance or user experience**


### Acceptance Criteria

* **AC1:** A telemetry library/service is successfully integrated into the Flutter application
* **AC2:** The system captures user events such as button clicks and screen navigation
* **AC3:** Application performance metrics (e.g., startup time, response time) are collected
* **AC4:** Device information (device model, OS version, app version) is captured
* **AC5:** Error logs and crash reports are recorded and accessible
* **AC6:** Telemetry data is securely transmitted to a backend server for storage and analysis
* **AC7:** User consent is obtained before collecting telemetry data, in compliance with privacy regulations
* **AC8:** Users can enable or disable telemetry collection via configuration settings
* **AC9:** Dashboards and reports are available for visualizing telemetry data
* **AC10:** Telemetry implementation does not significantly impact application performance or user experience

### Implementation Details

### **Architecture**

* Client-side telemetry module integrated within the Flutter app
* Backend telemetry ingestion service for data collection and storage
* Analytics and visualization layer for dashboards and reporting

### **Client-Side (Flutter)**

* Integration with telemetry/analytics SDKs such as:

  * Firebase Analytics / Crashlytics
  * OpenTelemetry (if standardized approach is preferred)
* Event tracking framework:

  * Structured event logging (event name, timestamp, metadata)
* Performance monitoring:

  * App startup time tracking
  * API latency measurement
* Error tracking:

  * Exception handling hooks
  * Crash reporting integration

### **Backend**

* Secure API endpoints for telemetry ingestion
* Data storage (e.g., Elasticsearch, BigQuery, or similar analytics store)
* Data processing pipelines for aggregation and analysis

### **Security & Privacy**

* Data encryption in transit (HTTPS) and at rest
* User consent management (opt-in/opt-out mechanism)
* Anonymization or pseudonymization of sensitive data
* Compliance with regulations (e.g., GDPR)

### **Configurability**

* Feature flags to enable/disable telemetry
* Configurable event tracking levels
* Environment-based configurations (dev, staging, production)

### **Performance Considerations**

* Asynchronous event logging
* Batching and throttling of telemetry data
* Minimal resource usage (CPU, memory, network)

### Mockups/Wireframes

### Ticket Contents

## Description
This feature enables OCR (Optical Character Recognition) integration within the Android Registration Client to automatically extract demographic information from identity documents during registration.

Currently, operators manually enter demographic details such as name, address, and date of birth, which is time-consuming and error-prone. This feature introduces document scanning via the device camera, followed by OCR-based text extraction and automatic pre-filling of form fields.

The goal is to reduce manual effort, improve data accuracy, and accelerate the registration workflow, while maintaining high standards of data security and configurability.


### Goals & Mid-Point Milestone

## Goals
**Overall Goals**

1. Enable document capture using Android device camera
2. Integrate OCR engine (on-device/server-based) for text extraction
3. Map extracted text to demographic fields
4. Auto-fill demographic form fields with extracted data
5. Provide confidence scores and visual indicators
6. Support multilingual OCR extraction
7. Ensure secure handling of captured and extracted data
8. Allow configuration of OCR behavior without code changes

**Mid-Point Milestone**

1. Camera-based document capture with image quality guidance (alignment, blur, lighting)
2. Basic OCR integration (single language support)
3. Extraction of core fields (Name, DOB, Gender)
4. Auto-fill of extracted fields into demographic form
5. Manual edit capability for extracted values
6. Basic error handling (OCR failure fallback to manual entry)


### Setup/Installation

_No response_

### Expected Outcome

The final product will provide a seamless, assisted data entry experience for registration operators:

1. Operators can scan identity documents directly within the app
2. The system intelligently extracts relevant demographic data using OCR
3. Extracted values are automatically populated into the appropriate fields
4. Each field displays a confidence score with visual indicators (Green/Yellow/Red) to guide operator validation
5. Operators retain full control to review, edit, or override extracted data
6. The system supports multiple languages, adapting to deployment-specific requirements
7. Robust error handling ensures fallback to manual entry when needed
8. All data handling complies with security, encryption, and privacy standards
9. The feature is highly configurable (document types, OCR engine, thresholds, storage policies)

Overall, the system will significantly reduce registration time, minimize errors, and improve operator efficiency and applicant experience.

AC6: OCR errors are handled gracefully with recapture and manual entry fallback options
AC7: All extracted data complies with encryption and security standards of the registration client
AC8: OCR configurations (document types, thresholds, engine selection) are adjustable without code changes


### 5. Implementation Details

1. Architecture

- Modular OCR integration layer to support:
  - On-device OCR (e.g., ML Kit / Tesseract)

  - Rule-based or template-based mapping of extracted text to:
    - Name
    - Address
    - DOB
    - Gender
    - Document Number
  - Configurable mapping rules
- Confidence Scoring
  - OCR engine-provided confidence scores
  - Threshold-based classification:
    - High (Green)
    - Medium (Yellow)
    - Low (Red)

  - Highlight low-confidence fields
  - Editable pre-filled fields
  - Error prompts and recapture options
- Error Handling
  - OCR failure detection
  - Partial extraction handling
  - Retry + fallback to manual entry

- Security & Privacy
  - End-to-end encryption of captured images and extracted data
  - Configurable storage policies for document images
  - No external data transfer unless server OCR is explicitly enabled
  - Compliance with MOSIP data protection standards
- Configurability
  - Feature flags for OCR enablement
  - Configurable:
    - OCR engine type (on-device/server)

title: Telemetry for Android Registration Client
content:
Problem description:
## **1. Ticket Contents: Description**

This feature focuses on implementing a **telemetry system within the Flutter-based Android Registration Client** to collect data on user behavior and application performance.

Currently, there is limited visibility into how users interact with the application and where performance issues may occur. By integrating telemetry, the system will enable **data-driven decision-making**, helping product and engineering teams identify usage patterns, detect bottlenecks, monitor crashes, and continuously improve the user experience.

The feature will ensure that telemetry data is collected securely, respects user privacy, and can be configured based on deployment needs.

## **2. Goals & Mid-Point Milestone**

### **Overall Goals**

* Integrate a telemetry library/service into the Flutter application
* Capture user interaction events (clicks, navigation, flows)
* Collect application performance metrics (startup time, response latency)
* Capture device metadata (model, OS version, app version)
* Log errors, exceptions, and crash reports
* Enable secure transmission of telemetry data to backend systems
* Ensure compliance with privacy regulations (user consent, opt-in/opt-out)
* Provide dashboards and reporting for analysis
* Ensure minimal performance overhead due to telemetry

### **Mid-Point Milestone (1.5 Months)**

* Basic telemetry SDK integration in Flutter app
* Capture core user events (screen navigation, key actions)
* Capture basic performance metrics (app startup time)
* Implement error and crash logging
* Backend endpoint integration for telemetry ingestion
* Basic configuration toggle to enable/disable telemetry

## **3. Expected Outcome**

The final implementation will provide a **robust and scalable telemetry framework** embedded within the Flutter application:

* The system will automatically capture and log **user interactions**, enabling visibility into user journeys and feature usage
* **Performance metrics** such as app startup time, API response times, and screen load times will be tracked continuously
* **Crash reports and error logs** will be collected to help quickly identify and debug issues
* Telemetry data will be **securely transmitted and stored** in backend systems for further analysis
* Users will have control over telemetry collection through **consent mechanisms and configuration settings**
* Product and engineering teams will be able to access **dashboards and reports** to analyze trends, detect anomalies, and make informed decisions
* The telemetry system will be optimized to ensure **no noticeable degradation in app performance or user experience**

## **4. Acceptance Criteria**

* **AC1:** A telemetry library/service is successfully integrated into the Flutter application
* **AC2:** The system captures user events such as button clicks and screen navigation
* **AC3:** Application performance metrics (e.g., startup time, response time) are collected
* **AC4:** Device information (device model, OS version, app version) is captured
* **AC5:** Error logs and crash reports are recorded and accessible
* **AC6:** Telemetry data is securely transmitted to a backend server for storage and analysis
* **AC7:** User consent is obtained before collecting telemetry data, in compliance with privacy regulations
* **AC8:** Users can enable or disable telemetry collection via configuration settings
* **AC9:** Dashboards and reports are available for visualizing telemetry data
* **AC10:** Telemetry implementation does not significantly impact application performance or user experience


## **5. Implementation Details**

### **Architecture**

* Client-side telemetry module integrated within the Flutter app
* Backend telemetry ingestion service for data collection and storage
* Analytics and visualization layer for dashboards and reporting

### **Client-Side (Flutter)**

* Integration with telemetry/analytics SDKs such as:

  * Firebase Analytics / Crashlytics
  * OpenTelemetry (if standardized approach is preferred)
* Event tracking framework:

  * Structured event logging (event name, timestamp, metadata)
* Performance monitoring:

  * App startup time tracking
  * API latency measurement
* Error tracking:

  * Exception handling hooks
  * Crash reporting integration

### **Backend**

* Secure API endpoints for telemetry ingestion
* Data storage (e.g., Elasticsearch, BigQuery, or similar analytics store)
* Data processing pipelines for aggregation and analysis

### **Security & Privacy**

* Data encryption in transit (HTTPS) and at rest
* User consent management (opt-in/opt-out mechanism)
* Anonymization or pseudonymization of sensitive data
* Compliance with regulations (e.g., GDPR)

### **Configurability**

* Feature flags to enable/disable telemetry
* Configurable event tracking levels
* Environment-based configurations (dev, staging, production)

### **Performance Considerations**

* Asynchronous event logging
* Batching and throttling of telemetry data
* Minimal resource usage (CPU, memory, network)

title: Enhanced Biometric Capture Validation with SDK Match Score & Face Quality Checks
content:
Problem description:
User Story: Enhanced Biometric Capture Validation with SDK Match Score & Face Quality Checks
As a Registration Operator
I want the system to show the biometric match score from the SDK along with the capture quality score, and automatically detect if the captured face image is non-smiling or low-quality
So that I can ensure the biometric is both high-quality and suitable for matching, ensuring accurate identification and a better applicant experience.

Problem / Need
Capturing a technically good biometric is not sufficient—identification accuracy depends on matchability (how well the biometric will match future samples) and image quality (clarity, lighting, pose, expression).

Operators currently see only quality scores.

They do not see matchability indicators, which help assess whether the captured biometric will perform well in deduplication or authentication.

For face capture, smiling, inconsistent lighting, tilt, or blur can make photos unusable.

The system needs to automatically detect such issues and guide operators for better captures.

This feature closes these gaps by combining Quality Score, Match Score, and Face Expression/Quality Validation.

Feature Description
1. SDK Match Score Display
After capturing biometrics (face, fingerprint, iris), the system sends the captured sample to the configured SDK (e.g., face SDK, fingerprint matcher).

SDK returns a Matchability Score such as:

Match Score (0–1 or 0–100)

Matching Confidence Level (Low/Medium/High)

Liveness or anti-spoof checks (if supported)

The system displays this along with the standard quality score.

Output Seen by Operator:
Quality Score (clarity, sharpness, positioning)

Match Score (SDK-based matchability)

Visual indicator:

Green: Good matchability

Yellow: Acceptable

Red: Poor / unusable

2. Non-Smiling Face Detection
Using face analytics from the SDK, the system detects:

Smile or unacceptable expressions

Mouth open

Eye closure / blink

Head tilt or rotation

If smiling or expressive face is detected:

UI shows:
“Neutral expression required. Please recapture the photo.”

3. Enhanced Face Image Quality Checks
For face captures, the system automatically validates:

Lighting uniformity

Background consistency

Sharpness & focus

Pose correctness (frontal, straight eyes, no tilt)

Occlusions (hair, mask, glasses glare)

If the face capture is poor, the system prompts the operator to retake it.

4. Display of Combined Validation Results
The capture screen will show:

Parameter | Displayed to Operator -- | -- Biometric Quality Score | Numeric + Pass/Fail Match Score | Numeric + Matchability rating Expression Check | Pass/Fail (e.g., “Neutral Face Required”) Photo Quality Indicators | Highlights issues: Blur / Lighting / Pose
Operators see all validations in one place.

5. Configurable Thresholds
Quality thresholds

Minimum match score

Expression rules (strict/relaxed)

Recapture enforcement (mandatory or override-allowed)

6. Storage in Packet
Store the quality score, match score, and face analysis metadata inside biometric packet metadata for audits and analytics.

Acceptance Criteria
AC1: System calculates and displays both quality score and SDK match score after capture.
AC2: System detects smiling or expressive faces and blocks capture until a neutral expression is provided.
AC3: System validates photo quality (lighting, focus, pose, occlusion) and prompts operator for correction.
AC4: System blocks operator from proceeding if match score < threshold (unless override enabled).
AC5: All scores and metadata are stored in the biometric packet.
AC6: Thresholds for match score and expression rules are configurable.
AC7: UI shows clear messages for each error or poor condition.
Example User Flow
Operator captures applicant’s face photo.

System calculates:

Quality score = 72 (Pass)

Match score = 48 (Below threshold 60 → Fail)

Expression: Smiling → Fail

Pose: Slight head tilt → Warning

System displays:

❌ Matchability too low. Please recapture.

❌ Neutral expression required.

⚠️ Head slightly tilted. Adjust camera.

Operator recaptures face.

New results:

Quality = 85 (Pass)

Match score = 78 (Pass)

Neutral expression (Pass)

Pose correct (Pass)

Operator proceeds.

title: Calculation of Quality Score
content:
Problem description:
User Story: Calculation of Quality Score

As a Registration Operator
I want the system to automatically calculate and display the quality score for each biometric modality captured
So that I can ensure the biometrics meet the minimum quality requirements before submitting the registration packet.

Problem / Need

Biometric capture quality varies based on lighting, sensor conditions, operator skill, and applicant posture. Poor-quality biometrics lead to high false match rates, delays in identity creation, and downstream failure in authentication or deduplication.

To improve data quality and ensure compliance with biometric standards (e.g., ISO/IEC 29794), the system must calculate, display, and enforce quality thresholds for fingerprints, face, and iris captures.

Feature Description

Automatic Quality Calculation
After capturing any biometric (fingerprint, iris, face), the system automatically triggers quality evaluation.

Quality score is calculated either by:

An internal MOSIP quality algorithm, or

A configured external third-party quality SDK (e.g., NFIQ2).

The calculation is real-time, with no manual intervention required.

Score & Status Output
The output includes:

Numerical score (e.g., 0–100 or SDK-specific range)

Pass/Fail status based on threshold

Optional granular metrics (contrast, sharpness, clarity, noise, focus, pose estimation)

Display to Operator
The UI shows:

A visual indicator (green/yellow/red)

The exact score

Pass/Fail message

If the quality is below threshold, a prompt instructs the operator to recapture.

Configurable Thresholds
Each biometric modality has its own configurable minimum score:

fingerprint.threshold

iris.threshold

face.threshold

Threshold values are controlled via configuration files or server-side policies.

Enforcement Logic
If score ≥ threshold → operator can proceed

If score < threshold → operator must recapture (configurable to allow override for exceptions)

Data Storage
The final quality score and status are stored as part of the biometric packet metadata.

Supports future audits and analytics.

Error Handling
If the quality calculation fails due to SDK error, device failure, or invalid inputs:

The system shows a clear error message

Allows retry or fallback to default device quality metrics

Acceptance Criteria
AC1: Automatic Trigger

Quality score calculation must start immediately after each biometric capture.

AC2: Valid Score Generation

The system must generate a numerical score and pass/fail decision.

AC3: Operator Visibility

The UI must clearly show the calculated score and its meaning.

AC4: Threshold Enforcement

Operators cannot proceed with low-quality biometrics unless override is enabled in configuration.

AC5: Modality Coverage

Quality scoring is supported for:

All fingerprint types (slap, thumb, rolled if applicable)

Iris captures

Face images

AC6: Storage

The system stores the quality score in the biometric packet.

AC7: Configurability

Administrators can modify thresholds without code changes.

AC8: Error Handling

Appropriate error messages and fallback logic must be provided.

Example User Flow

Operator captures a face image.

System calculates score: 62, threshold = 70 → FAIL

UI shows a red indicator and message:
“Face quality too low. Please recapture.”

Operator recaptures; new score = 78 → PASS

Operator proceeds to next step.

title: Blocklisted Words Validation Across Registration Workflow
content:
Problem description:
User Story: Blocklisted Words Validation Across Registration Workflow

As a Registration Operator
I want the system to detect and prevent the use of blocklisted or prohibited words in demographic fields and critical review screens
So that the registration data remains clean, valid, and free from abusive, offensive, or restricted terms before submission.

Problem / Need

During data entry, operators may intentionally or unintentionally enter inappropriate, offensive, or disallowed words in fields such as name, address, or remarks. These errors may go unnoticed and can compromise data quality, cause audit failures, or violate compliance norms.

To ensure clean and safe demographic data, the system must have built-in validation to prevent the use of such blocklisted words at every key stage of the registration process.

Feature Description

The feature introduces an automated blocklist validation system that checks for prohibited words across the following pages:

Demographic Details Page
When operators enter demographic information (Name, Address, Parents’ Names, etc.), the system automatically checks user input against the blocklisted words repository.

If any blocklisted word is detected:

The field is highlighted.

An inline error message appears:
“This entry contains a prohibited word. Please correct the input.”

Operator cannot proceed until correction is made.

Acknowledgement Page
Before generating the acknowledgement slip, the system performs a final validation across all demographic fields.

If blocklisted content is found:

A modal alert appears with the list of fields containing prohibited content.

Operator must correct the fields in the Demographic Details Page before generating the acknowledgement.

Packet Approval Page
During operator or supervisor approval of the packet:

The system performs a last-stage blocklist validation before the packet is marked approved.

If prohibited content exists:

Approval is blocked.

An error message appears:
“Packet cannot be approved. Please revise demographic details to remove prohibited content.”

The operator is redirected to the specific field to make corrections.

Configuration & Flexibility

The blocklisted words are maintained in a centrally configurable list (JSON/YAML or server-managed configuration).

The list can be updated without code changes.

Supports multiple languages and case-insensitive matching.

Acceptance Criteria
AC1: Blocklist Validation

The system checks all demographic fields against the configurable blocklisted words.

AC2: Input Restriction on Demographic Details Page

If an operator enters a blocklisted term, inline validation prevents moving to the next step.

AC3: Validation on Acknowledgement Page

Blocklisted terms are flagged during acknowledgement generation.

The system blocks slip generation until resolution.

AC4: Validation on Packet Approval Page

Packet cannot be approved if any demographic field still contains blocklisted content.

AC5: Clear User Feedback

UI must display clear, actionable messages specifying which field contains prohibited content.

AC6: Configurability

Blocklist must be editable without deployment or code modification.

Supports Unicode, multilingual entries, partial matches, and regex-based patterns (if applicable).

AC7: Logging & Auditing

Any attempt to save or approve data containing blocklisted terms is logged for auditing.

User Flow Example

Operator enters address: “123 Fake Street - Test BadWord Colony.”

System detects "BadWord" from blocklist → shows inline error → operator corrects the input.

At Acknowledgement page, system revalidates → all clean → slip generated.

During Packet Approval, system performs final check → approval allowed only if all fields pass validation.

Discussion and resolution:
[abd-RAHEEM]: Hi, I'd like to work on this issue.

I've gone through the feature description and acceptance criteria. Here's my proposed approach:

- Create a `BlocklistValidator` utility that loads the prohibited words list from a centrally configurable source (JSON/YAML or server-managed config), supporting case-insensitive and Unicode matching
- Hook inline validation into the demographic fields using onChanged callbacks on the form fields, highlighting the field and showing an inline error message on detection
- Add a final validation pass on the Acknowledgement Page before slip generation and on the Packet Approval Page before approval is marked, blocking both actions if prohibited content is found
- Use the existing audit/logging mechanism in the project to log any blocked attempt

Before I start, a couple of quick questions:
1. Is there an existing config mechanism I should plug the blocklist into, or should I introduce a new config key?
2. Is there a preferred audit service class already in use that I should route the logging through?

Happy to adjust the plan based on feedback.

title: Quality SDK: Support for 3rd party SDK to measure quality of biometrics captured
content:
Problem description:
User Story: Support for Third-Party SDKs to Measure Biometric Capture Quality

As a Registration Operator
I want the Registration Client to seamlessly integrate with third-party biometric quality assessment SDKs
So that the system can automatically evaluate the quality of captured biometrics (fingerprints, iris, face) and ensure they meet the required thresholds before submission.

Problem / Need

Biometric capture quality is critical for accurate deduplication and reliable identity creation. However, the existing workflow relies on device-specific quality checks or operator judgement, which may be inconsistent or insufficient.
To ensure high-quality, standards-compliant biometrics across all deployments, the Registration Client must support plug-and-play integration of industry-approved third-party quality assessment SDKs.

Feature Description

This feature introduces the ability for MOSIP Registration Client to:

Integrate with External Quality SDKs

Provide an extensible interface (adapter) that allows any compliant third-party biometric quality SDK (e.g., NFIQ/NFIQ2 for fingerprints, ISO/IEC quality algorithms) to be plugged in.

Ensure no tight coupling with any vendor implementation.

Trigger Quality Checks During Capture

After biometrics are captured (fingerprint slap, iris pair, or face image), the client automatically invokes the integrated SDK for quality scoring.

SDK returns a score and/or pass–fail results.

Display Quality Feedback to Operators

Operators see clear indicators (score, color coding, "Pass"/"Fail") immediately after capture.

If quality is below threshold, the operator is prompted to recapture.

Apply Configurable Thresholds

Administrators can define the minimum acceptable quality scores in configuration files or server-managed policies.

Thresholds may differ by biometric modality.

Record Quality Metadata

The quality score and related metrics from the SDK are stored as part of the biometric packet.

Supports auditing and future reference.

Fallback & Error Handling

If the SDK fails or is unavailable, the system falls back to default device quality checks (if enabled).

Appropriate warnings are shown to the operator.

Acceptance Criteria

AC1: The Registration Client can integrate with at least one external biometric quality SDK via a standardized interface.

AC2: Upon biometric capture, the SDK is automatically invoked, and the quality score is returned.

AC3: Operators see quality results in real-time with clear visual feedback.

AC4: The system blocks submission if the biometric quality is below the configured threshold (configurable behaviour).

AC5: Quality metadata is stored in the captured packet.

AC6: System handles SDK errors gracefully and provides fallback behaviour.

Examples of User Flow

Operator captures applicant’s fingerprints.

Registration Client sends the fingerprint data to the integrated SDK.

SDK returns: score=78, status="PASS" against threshold 70.

UI shows a green indicator → Operator proceeds.

For iris capture, SDK returns score=22, status="FAIL" against threshold 40.

UI prompts: “Low iris quality detected. Please recapture.”

title: <Performance Enhancement> Enable Key Manager to Support 500K Packet Processing per Day (MOSIP Release 1.4.x)
content:
Problem description:
### Description:
This task focuses on enhancing the performance of the Key Manager component in MOSIP to reliably support a target throughput of 500,000 packets per day. The objective is to optimize key management operations and system efficiency to handle sustained high-volume workloads without compromising security or stability.
The implementation involves identifying bottlenecks and applying optimizations across cryptographic operations, memory handling, caching, and concurrency management. These improvements will be validated through comprehensive performance testing to ensure the system meets the desired throughput benchmarks.
All validated changes should be merged into the release/1.4.x branch following standard review and release practices.

### Key Areas of Enhancement:
1. ThreadLocal JCA Object Reuse
JCA objects such as Cipher, KeyFactory, MessageDigest, SecureRandom, KeyGenerator, CertPathValidator, and CertificateFactory are expensive to instantiate due to provider lookups and SPI loading.
 - Introduced ThreadLocal caching to reuse these objects per thread and eliminate repeated allocations under concurrent load
- Applied across:
  - CryptoCore — Cipher, SecretKeyFactory, SecureRandom
  - ZKCryptoManagerServiceImpl — Cipher, MessageDigest
  - SignatureServiceImpl — KeyFactory, MessageDigest
  - RandomKeysGenerator — KeyGenerator, Cipher, SecureRandom
  - PartnerCertificateManagerServiceImpl — CertPathValidator, CertificateFactory
- Ensured proper cleanup using @PreDestroy to prevent memory leaks in thread-pooled environments
2. Multi-Layer Caching
- Implemented certificate path caching (Cache2k with TTL and ~2000 entries) to avoid repeated PKIX chain validations
- Introduced domain index caching using DN and SKI for constant-time issuer lookup
- Added ConcurrentHashMap-based caches in SignatureServiceImpl for:
  - Decoded PublicKey objects
  - Parsed X509Certificate objects
  - JWS headers
  - Certificate trust validation results
3. Byte Array Copy Optimization
- Replaced Arrays.copyOfRange() with System.arraycopy() in performance-critical paths
- Applied across components such as CryptomanagerServiceImpl, ClientCryptoFacade, SessionKeyDecryptorHelper, KeymanagerUtil, and CryptomanagerUtils
- Reduced unnecessary array allocations and minimized bounds-check overhead

### Acceptance Criteria:
- System successfully processes 500,000 packets per day under performance test conditions
- ThreadLocal reuse implemented and validated without memory leaks
- Multi-layer caching reduces redundant cryptographic and certificate validation overhead
- Byte array optimizations reduce memory footprint and improve execution speed
- Performance benchmarks demonstrate measurable improvement over baseline
- No functional or security regressions observed
- Code reviewed and merged into release/1.4.x branch
- Documentation updated to reflect performance enhancements and configurations

title: Enable MOSIP to support ECC Algorithm during encryption & decryption
content:
Problem description:
**Description:**
As an identity and access management system user, I want the MOSIP to support encryption and decryption using the ECC algorithm So that user credentials and sensitive data can be securely encrypted, transmitted, and decrypted to prevent unauthorised access.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. **ECC Encryption:** 
- The IDA module must allow encryption of sensitive auth data (e.g., auth request, otp, KYC data) using ECC public keys before transmitting data.

2. **ECC Decryption:**
- The IDA module must decrypt incoming encrypted data (auth request) using the ECC algorithm
- During KYC authentication decryption process must ensure that only authorized users with valid private keys can decrypt the data.

3. Authentication & Authorization:
- ECC encryption must be used during user authentication (e.g., signing or encrypting access tokens) to ensure that only legitimate users gain access to resources.
- The IDA module must verify digital signatures using ECC during authorization to validate requests and responses.

4. **Error Handling & Security Alerts:**
- The system must provide clear error messages when ECC encryption or decryption fails, without exposing sensitive details.

5. **Compliance & Auditability:**
- Encryption and decryption events should be logged for audit purposes, ensuring traceability and accountability in the identity and access lifecycle.

6. Backward Compatibility:
- Enabling system to sign downloaded UIN with RSA, ECC, Eddsa Algorithm

7. Migration Compatibility:
- Allowing the users to switch between RSA, ECC and Eddsa (Xdh - for encryption/decryption)

title: R&D on Quantum-Resistant Cryptography Adoption in Key Manager
content:
Problem description:
**Title:** 
Research and prototype integration of quantum-safe crypto algorithms (Kyber, Dilithium, SPHINCS+) in Key Manager

As a security architect or cryptography engineer I want to conduct R&D to evaluate and prototype the adoption of quantum-safe cryptographic algorithms —  Kyber, Dilithium , and SPHINCS within the Key Manager component So that our system can be prepared for post-quantum security and ensure long-term cryptographic resilience against quantum attacks.

**Description**
This R&D aims to explore the integration of post-quantum cryptographic (PQC) algorithms  (Kyber, Dilithium, SPHINCS+) into the existing Key Manager service. The effort includes identifying available libraries, assessing compatibility with the Java  21 tech stack, and designing a prototype implementation.

**Key outcomes expected include:**
- Comparative analysis of at least two Java-compatible PQC libraries (license, maturity, performance, native deps).
- Working Java 21 prototypes for Kyber, Dilithium and SPHINCS+ demonstrating key lifecycle + crypto operations.
- HSM support plan and prototype integration
- Integration using PKCS#11 or Java JCE provider interfaces.
- Performance benchmarks (key sizes, generation, sign/verify, encrypt/decrypt timings) and memory/CPU observations.
- Security / compliance assessment
- Documents: R&D summary, technical design for integration into Key Manager, and an upgrade/migration guide.

**Acceptance Criteria**

1. Library Evaluation
      Identify and document at least two stable Java-compatible PQC libraries (e.g., BouncyCastle PQC, OpenQuantumSafe bindings, LibOQS-JNI).
      Evaluate license, performance, and implementation maturity for each.
2. Algorithm Coverage
        Demonstrate basic use of:
          - Kyber 
          - Dilithium 
          - SPHINCS+ 
        Each demo must include sample inputs and expected outputs.
3. Prototype Implementation
    - Implement Java 21 prototypes (non-production sandbox) inside a Key Manager test module for:
             - Key generation.
             - Secure storage and retrieval (in-memory and simulated persistent store).
             - Sign and verify (Dilithium, SPHINCS+).
             - Encrypt / decrypt or KEM flows (Kyber).
4. Integration Feasibility
        - Produce a technical integration plan showing:
                 - How PQC primitives map to existing Key Manager interfaces (KeyPairGenerator, Signature-like APIs, Cipher/KEM-like APIs).
                 - JCE provider integration strategy (wrap PQC libs as a JCE provider or use existing providers).
                 - PKCS#11 / HSM interaction approach and required vendor considerations.
       - Provide performance benchmark table (key sizes, generation time, sign/verify/encrypt/decrypt latency, memory footprint) with comparison to RSA/ECC equivalents.
5. HSM & JCE/PKCS#11 Support
       - Demonstrate or provide a clear prototype path to enable HSM support:
               - Show how to expose PQC keys via PKCS#11 slots assuming HSM vendor support and document required PKCS#11 extensions or limitations.
               - Provide JCE integration plan so existing Key Manager APIs (keyGen, encrypt/decrypt, sign/verify) continue to work with PQC keys with minimal changes.
               - Identify and document any native/JNI dependencies and fallback (software) implementations when HSM lacks PQC support.
6. Security & Compliance
        - Provide NIST PQC standardization assessment — indicate how chosen parameter sets align with NIST recommendations as of the R&D date.
        - Document key sizes, expected security levels and cryptographic assumptions.
        - Identify any third-party dependencies with security risk (e.g., native libs, JNI) and mitigation.
7. Deliverable
         - Submit R&D summarizing findings, 
         - Prototype artifacts (code, build instructions, tests).
         - Technical design document for production integration.
         - Upgrade/migration document covering steps to adopt PQC in Key Manager and HSM considerations.

**Tasks**
1. Research Phase
    - Review NIST PQC outcomes and relevant publications for Kyber/Dilithium/SPHINCS+.
    - Identify Java 21 compatible PQC libraries and bindings (list ≥2).
    - Create evaluation matrix (license, maturity, JNI/native, API surface).
2. Environment Setup
    - Create isolated Key Manager sandbox project (Java 21).
    - Add build scripts (Maven/Gradle) to import PQC libraries and test harness.
    - Prepare test vectors and example messages.
3. Prototype Development
    - Implement Kyber KEM flows (keygen, encapsulate/decapsulate) in sandbox.
    - Implement Dilithium.
    - Implement SPHINCS+.
    - Integrate basic key lifecycle (generate, store, retrieve) using existing Key Manager abstractions.
4. JCE / PKCS#11 / HSM Integration
    - Design and implement a JCE adapter or provider wrapper for the chosen PQC library.
    - Build a PKCS#11 shim/proxy or use a simulated PKCS#11 provider for testing.
    - Attempt HSM vendor integration checklist: vendor PQC support, PKCS#11 extensions, firmware constraints.
5. Documentation
     - Produce technical design doc: API changes (if any), JCE provider plan, PKCS#11/HSM integration notes, migration strategy.
     - Produce upgrade document with step-by-step instructions to bring PQC into production, including fallback paths and dual-stack migration (PQ+classical hybrid signatures/encryption).

title: Admin module not working due to missing trust for corporate CA (Keycloak TLS / JWKS / token endpoint) (v3)
content:
Problem description:
My sandbox installation uses an ingress certificate signed by our organisation's internal CA. It has turned out that the admin module has its problems when running without public certificates. 

The first obstacle is login. After having entered `globaluser` and password, this error is displayed in the browser:
```
{"id":null,"version":null,"responsetime":"2026-04-01T11:19:39.560Z","metadata":null,"response":null,"errors":[{"errorCode":"KER-MSD-500","message":"Both provided Keys cannot be null."}]}
```

The main reason seems to be that my ingress certificate presented by the external IAM URL is unknown to the JVM in which admin-service runs. Having successfully worked around this, I found that token issuer comparison was unsuccessful.

Long story short, it looks like currently MOSIP's v3 deployment is not ready for such scenarios out of the box. I really think it should be (and this should also be verified by QA), because sandbox installations using internal CAs can be assumed to be a rather common scenario.

I have eventually succeded in getting the admin UI to work. For your reference, here's what I did (and I cannot rule out some of these steps being unnecessary):

**1. Change the configuration in admin-default.properties**

```diff
diff --git a/admin-default.properties b/admin-default.properties
index 2548bc7d..2954c663 100644
--- a/admin-default.properties
+++ b/admin-default.properties
@@ -208,7 +208,7 @@ mosip.iam.module.login_flow.response_type=code
 mosip.iam.authorization_endpoint=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/auth
 mosip.iam.module.admin_realm_id=mosip
 mosip.iam.token_endpoint=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/token
-mosip.iam.certs_endpoint=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/certs
+mosip.iam.certs_endpoint=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip/protocol/openid-connect/certs

 regproc.token.request.appid=regproc
 regproc.token.request.clientId=mosip-regproc-client
@@ -221,7 +221,8 @@ KEYBASEDTOKENAPI=${mosip.kernel.authmanager.url}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/cli
 mosip.iam.adapter.appid=admin
 mosip.iam.adapter.clientid=mosip-admin-client
 mosip.iam.adapter.clientsecret=${mosip.admin.client.secret}
-mosip.iam.adapter.issuerURL=${keycloak.internal.url}/auth/realms/mosip
+mosip.iam.adapter.issuerURL=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip
+mosip.keycloak.issuerUrl=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip
 mosip.authmanager.client-token-endpoint=${mosip.kernel.authmanager.url}/v1/authmanager/authenticate/clientidsecretkey
 # in minutes
 mosip.iam.adapter.validate-expiry-check-rate=1440
@@ -229,6 +230,7 @@ mosip.iam.adapter.validate-expiry-check-rate=1440
 mosip.iam.adapter.renewal-before-expiry-interval=1440
 #this should be false if you don?t use this restTemplate true if you do
 mosip.iam.adapter.self-token-renewal-enable=true
+auth-token-generator.rest.issuerUrl=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/mosip

 # LostRid
 mosip.registration.processor.lostrid.id=mosip.registration.lostrid
@@ -277,6 +279,8 @@ mosip.kernel.jsonvalidator.file-storage-uri=LOCAL

 mosip.kernel.machineid.length=5
 auth.server.admin.issuer.uri=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/
+auth.server.admin.issuer.internal.uri=${keycloak.external.url}/auth/realms/
+auth.server.admin.issuer.domain.validate=false
 MACHINE_GET_API=${mosip.kernel.masterdata.url}/v1/masterdata/machines/mappedmachines/
 CRYPTOMANAGERDECRYPT_API=${mosip.kernel.keymanager.url}/v1/keymanager/decrypt
 CRYPTOMANAGER_DECRYPT=${mosip.kernel.keymanager.url}/v1/keymanager/decrypt

```

**2. Create file with our certificate chain**

This file will need to be made known to the admin-service JVM before it starts. We will "inject" it later:
```shell
cat my-ingress-host.cer our-corporate-ca.pem >corp-ca-chain.pem
```

**3. Patch the helm installation for an initContainer to the admin-service deployment**

Install `kustomize` on your local host:
```shell
dnf install -y kustomize
```

Create a `post-render.sh` script:
```shell
#!/bin/bash

command -V kustomize >/dev/null || { echo "Error, 'kustomize' command is not installed on your local system." 1>&2; exit 1; }

set -euo pipefail

tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' EXIT

# Save helm output
cat > "$tmp/rendered.yaml"

# Copy kustomize files next to rendered.yaml
cp ./kustomization.yaml "$tmp/kustomization.yaml"

# Build patched output
kustomize build "$tmp"
```

Create a `kustomization.yaml` file:
```yaml
apiVersion: kustomize.config.k8s.io/v1beta1
kind: Kustomization

resources:
  - rendered.yaml

patches:
  - target:
      kind: Deployment
      name: admin-service
    patch: |-
      apiVersion: apps/v1
      kind: Deployment
      metadata:
        name: admin-service
      spec:
        template:
          spec:
            volumes:
              - name: corporate-ca
                secret:
                  secretName: corporate-ca
              - name: java-truststore
                emptyDir: {}
            initContainers:
              - name: import-corporate-ca
                image: eclipse-temurin:21-jre
                command:
                  - /bin/sh
                  - -c
                  - |
                    set -e
                    cp /opt/java/openjdk/lib/security/cacerts /work/cacerts
                    keytool -importcert \
                      -alias corporate-ca \
                      -file /ca/corp-ca.crt \
                      -keystore /work/cacerts \
                      -storepass changeit \
                      -noprompt
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: corporate-ca
                    mountPath: /ca
                    readOnly: true
                  - name: java-truststore
                    mountPath: /work
            containers:
              - name: admin-service
                env:
                  - name: JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
                    value: >-
                      -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStore=/work/cacerts
                      -Djavax.net.ssl.trustStorePassword=changeit
                volumeMounts:
                  - name: java-truststore
                    mountPath: /work
```

Patch `install.sh` to (a) create a `secret` from the above `.pem` file and (b) activate post-render for the `admin-service` installation:
```diff
diff --git a/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh b/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
index 9a08a24a..e450773f 100755
--- a/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
+++ b/deployment/v3/mosip/admin/install.sh
@@ -18,6 +18,15 @@ function installing_admin() {
   kubectl label ns $NS istio-injection=enabled --overwrite
   helm repo update

+  if [ -r ../corp-ca-chain.pem ]; then
+    echo "File '../corp-ca-chain.pem' found, preparing for sandbox installation with internal CA root."
+    kubectl -n admin delete secret corporate-ca 2>/dev/null || /bin/true
+    kubectl -n admin create secret generic corporate-ca --from-file=corp-ca.crt=../corp-ca-chain.pem || errorExit "Error creating 'corporate-ca' secret."
+    ADMIN_SERVICE_HELM_POST_RENDER='--post-renderer ./post-render.sh'
+  else
+    echo "No file '../corp-ca-chain.pem' found, assuming non-sandbox install."
+  fi
+
   echo Copy configmaps
   sed -i 's/\r$//' copy_cm.sh
   ./copy_cm.sh
@@ -32,7 +41,7 @@ function installing_admin() {
   helm -n $NS install admin-hotlist mosip/admin-hotlist --version $CHART_VERSION

   echo Installing admin service. Will wait till service gets installed.
-  helm -n $NS install admin-service mosip/admin-service --set istio.corsPolicy.allowOrigins\[0\].prefix=https://$ADMIN_HOST --wait --version $CHART_VERSION
+  helm -n $NS install admin-service mosip/admin-service --set istio.corsPolicy.allowOrigins\[0\].prefix=https://$ADMIN_HOST --wait --version $CHART_VERSION $ADMIN_SERVICE_HELM_POST_RENDER

   echo Installing admin-ui
   helm -n $NS install admin-ui mosip/admin-ui --set admin.apiUrl=https://$API_HOST/v1/ --set istio.hosts\[0\]=$ADMIN_HOST --version $CHART_VERSION
```

Note that the `corp-ca-chain.pem` file is expected to reside in the `mosip-infra/deployment/v3/mosip` directory, because I assume that this problem will eventually also need to be fixed for other MOSIP modules, too.

Discussion and resolution:
[mbert]: I noticed that I filed this issue in the wrong repo, should have gone to `mosip-infra`. I am closing this and have opened the issue in [the mosip-infra repo](https://github.com/mosip/mosip-infra/issues/1713). Sorry for the confusion.

title: Install in logging/ - inconsistent to documentation and not working for rke1 clusters, istio-addons-values.yaml broken
content:
Problem description:
The `install.sh` script tries to install `rancher-logging-crd` and `rancher-logging`. According to the documentation on docs.mosip.io this was to be installed through the Rancher UI. However the `logging` charts are no longer exposed in the Rancher UI for versions from 2.8.x which is why it makes sense to use `install.sh` for this. But here we need to specify a version, because an `rke1` cluster requires quite old docker and kubernetes versions. Hence we need to enforce using a version that works with these. 

Also the `rancher-logging` chart requires some additional arguments in order to work with an `rke1` cluster.

Second issue: in the file `istio-addons-values.yaml` the hostname `kibana.sandbox.xyz.net` is hardcoded and not replaced. It should be configured by `install.sh` (my example below edits the file automatically which is probably not ideal since that file is under version control, so you may want to make `istio-addons-values.yaml` a template from which you expand and generate the actual file).

This is what worked for me (note that some of the stuff below is only for `rke1` clusters):
```
diff --git a/logging/install.sh b/logging/install.sh
index 21b54dd..36aced8 100755
--- a/logging/install.sh
+++ b/logging/install.sh
@@ -24,6 +24,10 @@ function check_and_update_kibana_host() {
   # Store Kibana Host in a ConfigMap for easy retrieval
   kubectl -n $NS create configmap kibana-config --from-literal=mosip_kibana_host=$KIBANA_HOST --dry-run=client -o yaml | kubectl apply -f -
   echo "Kibana Host stored in ConfigMap: kibana-config"
+
+  # Fix default host name in istio-addons-values.yaml
+  sed -i "s/^\( *\)host:.*/\1host: $KIBANA_HOST/" istio-addons-values.yaml
+  echo "Kibana Host fixed in istio-addons-values.yaml"
 }
 
 check_and_update_kibana_host
@@ -32,6 +36,7 @@ function installing_logging() {
   echo Updating helm repos
   helm repo add bitnami https://charts.bitnami.com/bitnami
   helm repo add banzaicloud-stable https://charts.helm.sh/stable
+  helm repo add rancher-charts https://charts.rancher.io
   helm repo update
 
   echo Installing Bitnami Elasticsearch and Kibana istio objects
@@ -53,10 +58,12 @@ function installing_logging() {
   helm -n $NS install istio-addons mosip/istio-addons --version $ISTIO_ADDONS_CHART_VERSION -f istio-addons-values.yaml
 
   echo Installing crds for logging operator
-  helm -n $NS install rancher-logging-crd mosip/rancher-logging-crd --wait
+  helm -n $NS install rancher-logging-crd rancher-charts/rancher-logging-crd --version 106.0.4+up4.10.0-rancher.9 --wait
   echo Installed crds for logging operator
   echo Installing logging operator
-  helm -n $NS install rancher-logging mosip/rancher-logging -f values.yaml
+  helm -n $NS install rancher-logging rancher-charts/rancher-logging --version 106.0.4+up4.10.0-rancher.9 -f values.yaml \
+    --set additionalLoggingSources.rke.enabled=true \
+    --set additionalLoggingSources.rke2.enabled=false
   echo Installed logging operator
   return 0
 }
```

title: Keycloak SAML client integration into Rancher (observation cluster) does not work as documented
content:
Problem description:
Setup as described in the documentation:

**Keycloak side**

1. Make sure the admin user has a full name and an email address [1]
2. Create a SAML client with only "Sign Documents" and "Sign Assertions" ON, Client ID: <rancher-baseURL>/v1-saml/keycloak/saml/metadata, Valid Redirect URI: <rancher-baseURL>/v1-saml/keycloak/saml/acs [2]
3. Add all Builtin Protocol Mappers [2]
4. Not mentioned (but it should!), but leads to errors if omitted: change the attribute values so that the match what needs to be entered into Rancher [1]
5. Create a new "Group List" mapper and set the Group attribute name to "member" [2]
6. Create a User Property mapper "username" with Name, Property, Friendly Name, SAML Attribute Name "username" [1]
7. Navigate to Realm Settings / General, click "SMAL 2.0 Identity Provider Metadata" and copy the XML to the clipboard [2]
8. log out of Keycloak

**Rancher side**

1. Fill in the form for adding a Keycloak SAML Auth Provider as described in [1]
2. Submit the form.
3. Enter Keycloak admin credentials.

**Result**

In the popup various, like:
- "An error occurred logging in: Invalid saml attributes"
- An error occurred logging in: An error occurred logging in. Please try again.

In the Auth Provider form: "Access was not authorized"

Sometimes the auth provider turns out to be enabled anyway, only a little later.
Usually it does not. 

The method should really be documented all in one place (see #174), but also it should really work.

[1] from https://github.com/mosip/k8s-infra/blob/main/apps/keycloak/README.md
[2] from https://ranchermanager.docs.rancher.com/how-to-guides/new-user-guides/authentication-permissions-and-global-configuration/authentication-config/configure-keycloak-saml

Keycloak version (installed via helm): 16.1.1
Rancher version (installed via helm): v2.8.3

title: Integration of Keycloak and Rancher UI is a manual process and very error-prone
content:
Problem description:
The documentation apps/keycloak/README.md is a bit problematic in several ways.

1. It is a manual process. In both, Keycloak and Rancher, complex configuration needs to be entered in the respective web UIs. If any mistake is made the process will not succeed, and no help is provided in tracking down the source of the problem. Hence: this process really needs some automation. 
2. The documentation is fragmented. There is a link to the Rancher documentation and some additional remarks underneath. This even increases the likeliness of errors. Even at the risk of doing additional copy-paste, at the least we should have one comprehensive step-by-step guide to the process.

title: UI/UX Redesign Task – Resident Portal
content:
Problem description:
### Title
Redesign MOSIP Resident Portal for improved usability, accessibility, and inclusivity aligned with GenderMag & Sensemaking (SenseMag) principles

### Background & Context
The MOSIP Resident Portal is a self-service web application that enables residents to manage their identity (UIN/VID), update data, track requests, and access services.
It includes features such as:
- Dashboard with key services
- UIN services (history, VID management, secure ID, etc.)
- Data sharing and updates
- Notifications, profile, multilingual support
- While functionally rich, the current experience:
- Feels feature-heavy and workflow-fragmented
- Lacks intuitive navigation and interaction patterns
- Needs stronger accessibility and inclusivity alignment

### Objective
Redesign the Resident Portal to be:
- User-friendly and intuitive
- Accessible and inclusive (GenderMag & SenseMag compliant)
- Modern, interactive, and scalable
- Aligned with real user mental models and workflows

### Scope (Pages to Redesign)
The designer should redesign end-to-end experience, including:
1. Entry & Navigation
- Login / Authentication flows (OTP, biometrics, etc.)
- Consent screen
- Global navigation (menu, header, profile, language)

2. Dashboard
- Overview of key services
- Notifications & activity feed
- Personalization

3. UIN Services
- View History
- Manage VID
- Secure My ID
- Track Requests
- Get Personalized Card
- Share My Data
- Update My Data

4. Informational Services
- Registration Centers
- Supporting Documents

5. Utility Flows
- Get My UIN
- Verify Email/Phone
- Appointment Booking

6. Profile & Settings
- User profile
- Language preferences
- Accessibility settings

### Key Design Principles
1. Usability & Clarity
- Reduce cognitive load
- Clear task-based navigation (not system-based)
- Progressive disclosure for complex actions

2. GenderMag Alignment
Ensure design supports diverse cognitive styles:
- Support risk-averse users (clear confirmations, undo options)
- Provide step-by-step guidance
- Avoid over-reliance on exploration-based learning
- Use clear, non-technical language

3. Sensemaking (SenseMag) Alignment
- Help users understand:
  - Where they are
  - What they can do
  - What just happened
- Strong feedback loops
- Clear system status visibility

4. Accessibility (Critical)
- Color contrast, readable typography
- Keyboard navigation
- Screen reader compatibility
- Multi-language support (already supported but needs UX refinement)
- Align with MOSIP Design theme

5. Interaction & ExperienceMicro-interactions for feedback
- Guided workflows (especially for complex flows like data update)
- Visual hierarchy and prioritisation

### Expected Deliverables
- Design Artifacts
  - User flows (current vs improved)
  - Information architecture (IA)
  - Wireframes (low fidelity)
  - High-fidelity UI designs
  - Interactive prototypes (Figma preferred)
- UX Enhancements
  - Journey maps for key tasks:
  - Update data
  - Manage VID
  - Track request
  - Pain point identification + improvements
- Accessibility Deliverables
  - Accessibility checklist
  - Color palette with contrast validation
  - Typography scale
- Design System Alignment
  - Component library (buttons, cards, forms, alerts)
  - Reusable patterns for:
  - Forms
  - Status tracking
  - Notifications

### Acceptance Criteria
- Users can complete key tasks (e.g., update data, track request) in ≤ 3–5 steps
- Navigation is task-oriented, not feature-oriented
- All flows provide clear feedback and status visibility
- Demonstrates GenderMag alignment:
   - Clear instructions
   - Reduced ambiguity
   - Confidence-building UX
- Improved engagement and usability (qualitative testing)

### Non-Functional Requirements
- Responsive design (mobile + tablet + desktop)
- Performance-friendly UI (lightweight components)
- Scalable for future services
- Localization-ready

### Suggested Enhancements 
- Introduce “Guided Mode” for first-time users
- Add task-based dashboard (e.g., “What do you want to do?”)
- Use status trackers (progress bars for requests)
- Add contextual help/tooltips
- Introduce visual service cards instead of text-heavy lists

### References
- Existing Portal: https://resident.collab.mosip.net/#/dashboard
- MOSIP Documentation (features & flows)

Discussion and resolution:

title: Feature: Allow resident services to log in even when all the modalities are locked
content:
Problem description:
Add Support for allowing locked Authentication Types to Login to Resident Portal.

Problem statement: When Resident lock the all authentication types resident will not be able to unlock any Authentication Types back again as they are not allowed for login into resident portal itself. 

Solution:

If  resident is allowed to login to selected authentication types though it is locked for other partners, user will be able to login to resident portal and unlock any authentication types back. So this will happen on specific authentication types after user gives their consent by selecting the specific authentication types for excluding resident portal from the authentication lock validation.



Steps:

Authentication type locking with exclusion for resident portal login:



Authentication in IDA after the exclusion for resident partner:



Changes needed:

ID Repo:

Accept lockExcludedAuthPartners=["resident-partner"] for locked Auth Types in the Auth Type Lock API. 

Add a column in uin_auth_lock table called lockExcludedAuthPartners VarChar(256), nullable. Update in both db scripts and update/rollback scripts. 

Probagate lockExcludedAuthPartners=["resident-partner"] for locked Auth Types to IDA as part of websub event.

IDA:

Accept lockExcludedAuthPartners=["resident-partner"] for locked Auth Types in the websub event. 

Add a column in uin_auth_lock table called lockExcludedAuthPartners VarChar(256), nullable. Update in both db scripts and update/rollback scripts. 

During any Authentication, check if the Auth Type is having exclusion of the incoming partner ID.

Resident Service (endpoint- /resident/v1/auth-lock-unlock):

Send lockExcludedAuthPartners attribute to ID Repo for the lock excluded Auth Types, lockExcludedAuthPartners=["resident-partner"] . Here the resident-partner ID needs to come from the resident service configuration mosip-resident-service-partner-id. This needs to be configured as part of resident oidc client on boarding script. (It should be informed to the devops team to update the on boarding script to additionally set this property. ) 

The sets of Auth Types that can be Excluded as above in the UI should come from a Resident Service configuration. ( resident.auth-types-groups.exclusion-for-resident-login=["otp-email","otp-phone","bio-Finger", "bio-Iris", "bio-Face"]  ) . Note here demo is not in the exclusion set.  So no validation is performed on that. This property should be optional and if it is not there it should behave like earlier.

DevOps (onboarding script):

It should be informed to the devops team to update the on boarding script to additionally set the property as explained under Resident-service section.

Descoped: 

Resident UI: (Descoped)

Add Option on Lockable Auth Type for "Exclude for Resident Portal Login".

The sets of Auth Types that can be Excluded as above in the UI should come from a Resident Service configuration. ( resident.auth-types-groups.exclusion-for-resident-login=["otp-email","otp-phone","bio-Finger", "bio-Iris", "bio-Face"]  ) . Note here demo is not in the exclusion set.  So no validation is performed on that.

Whenever user locks an authentication type within an exclusion set, by default it can be marked for exclusion by the UI. But resident should be able to unselect which Auth types he/she doesn't to exclude in that set provided at least one of them is kept for the exclusion. 

Whenever any auth type is locked the option for excluding it for resident portal login should not be shown. 

Validate if All Auth Types locked in each exclusion set, atleast one Auth type is selected among them for "Exclude for Resident Portal Login".

On submission, send excludeLockForResidentLogin=true for the selected AuthTypes Locking selections. For unlocked Auth Types this flag should be set to null.

title: ES-2818: eSignet Mock – Biometric options not displayed during biometric login even after running Mock MDS
content:
Problem description:
## *Description:*

In *eSignet Mock*, when attempting to log in using *Biometric authentication*, the biometric options (fingerprint/face/iris, as applicable) are *not displayed*, even after successfully running the *Mock MDS (Mock Device Service)*.

## *Steps to Reproduce:*

1. *Start the* *Mock MDS* *service.*

1. *Launch* *eSignet Mock**.*

1. *Navigate to* *Login → Biometric Authentication**.*

1. *Observe the available biometric options.*

## *Actual Result:*

Biometric options are *not displayed* in the login screen, even though Mock MDS is running.

## *Expected Result:*

Biometric options should be displayed and available for selection once Mock MDS is running.

![image-20260202-070552.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2818)

## 🔗 Linked Issues

### ISSUE
- **ES-2824**
  Status: New

## 📎 Attachments

- [image-20260202-070552.png](https://mosip.atlassian.net/browse/ES-2818)

Discussion and resolution:
[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Zeeshan Mehboob commented: This isn’t actually an issue. Chromium and Firefox have introduced certain rules and fixes that control whether an HTTPS application can make API calls to localhost or loopback addresses.

When such a request is made, the browser prompts the user to allow or block the access. If the user doesn’t choose “Allow,” the browser automatically disables the API call. In other words, the decision is entirely in the user’s hands.

Since the biometric API from the mock MDS runs on a loopback address, this behavior occurs. However, once the user selects “Allow,” everything works smoothly.

Another bug has been raised to check on this issue, we have to connect for this thing in next engg. review call as well.

[exalate-issue-sync[bot]]: Prathmesh Jadhav commented: Currently, we are unable to verify the issue because in ESQA2 we cannot test the login using Bio. A bug has been raised for this.- [https://github.com/mosip/esignet/issues/1802|https://github.com/mosip/esignet/issues/1802|smart-link] 

As we are unable to verify, re-opening the bug. once the Login with Bio is working, will re-test the bug.
